title.zh: 卷一百四十九 列傳第三十六: 耶律留哥 劉伯林 郭寶玉 石天應 移剌揑兒 耶律禿花 王珣
title.en: Volume 149 Biographies 36: Yelu Liuge, Liu Bolin, Guo Baoyu, Shi Tianying, Yi Lanieer, Yelu Tuhua, Wang Xun
title.raw: 卷一百四十九 列傳第三十六: 耶律留哥 劉伯林 郭寶玉 石天應 移剌揑兒 耶律禿花 王珣 Volume 149 Biographies 36: Yelu Liuge, Liu Bolin, Guo Baoyu, Shi Tianying, Yi Lanieer, Yelu Tuhua, Wang Xun

sentences.zh: 耶律留哥

translations.literal: Yelu Liuge
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Liuge

sentences.zh: 耶律留哥，契丹人，仕金為北邊千戶。

translations.literal: Yelu Liuge was a Khitan who served the Jin as a chiliarch on the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Liuge was a Khitan who held the rank of chiliarch on the Jin dynasty's northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 太祖起兵朔方，金人疑遼遺民有他志，下令遼民一戶，以二女真戶夾居防之。

translations.literal: When the Taizu raised troops in the northern regions, the Jurchens suspected that surviving subjects of Liao harbored other intentions, and ordered that each Liao household be sandwiched between two Jurchen households for surveillance.
translations.idiomatic: When Genghis Khan rose in arms from the north, the Jin suspected that remaining Liao subjects might harbor disloyal ambitions. They decreed that every Liao household be flanked on either side by two Jurchen households as a guard against sedition.

sentences.zh: 留哥不自安。

translations.literal: Liuge could not feel at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Liuge felt increasingly insecure under this arrangement.

sentences.zh: 歲壬申，遁至隆安、韓州，糾壯士剽掠其地。

translations.literal: In the year renshen, he fled to Long'an and Hanzhou, gathered stalwart men, and raided those regions.
translations.idiomatic: In the renshen year (1212), he fled to Long'an and Hanzhou, rallied bold fighting men, and began raiding the countryside.

sentences.zh: 州發卒追捕，留哥皆擊走之。

translations.literal: The prefectures sent troops in pursuit; Liuge beat them all back.
translations.idiomatic: When the prefectures dispatched soldiers to hunt him down, Liuge routed every force sent against him.

sentences.zh: 因與耶的合勢募兵，數月衆至十餘萬，推留哥為都元帥，耶的副之，營帳百里，威震遼東。

translations.literal: Thereupon he joined forces with Yede to recruit troops; within months the multitude reached more than a hundred thousand. They made Liuge supreme commander with Yede as his deputy; their camps stretched for a hundred li, and their prestige shook Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: He then allied with Yede to raise an army. Within a few months their following swelled to over a hundred thousand men. Liuge was acclaimed supreme commander, with Yede as his second. Their encampments stretched a hundred li, and their power thundered across Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 太祖命按陳那衍、渾都古行軍至遼，遇之，問所從來，留哥對曰：「我契丹軍也，往附大國，道阻馬疲，故逗遛於此。」

translations.literal: The Taizu ordered Anchanna and Hondugu to march an army into Liao territory. They encountered him and asked whence he came. Liuge replied: "I am a Khitan army, going to submit to the Great State. The road is blocked and our horses are worn, so we have delayed here."
translations.idiomatic: Genghis Khan ordered Anchanna and Hondugu to lead troops into Liao territory. When they met Liuge, they asked where he was headed. Liuge answered: "We are a Khitan army bound to submit to your great realm. Our road has been blocked and our horses exhausted, so we have halted here."

sentences.zh: 按陳曰：「我奉旨討女真，適與爾會，庸非天乎！

translations.literal: Anchanna said: "I have received orders to punish the Jurchens, and it happens that I meet you—is this not Heaven's doing!
translations.idiomatic: Anchanna said: "I have been commanded to subdue the Jurchens, and to meet you just now—can this be anything but Heaven's design?

sentences.zh: 然爾欲效順，何以為信？」

translations.literal: Yet if you wish to show obedience, what shall serve as proof?"
translations.idiomatic: But if you truly mean to submit, what pledge will you give as proof?"

sentences.zh: 留哥乃率所部會按陳于金山，刑白馬、白牛，登高北望，折矢以盟。

translations.literal: Liuge then led his forces to meet Anchanna at Jinshan, slaughtered a white horse and white ox, climbed high and looked north, and broke arrows to seal the covenant.
translations.idiomatic: Liuge then led his troops to Jinshan to join Anchanna. They sacrificed a white horse and a white ox, climbed a height to look north, and broke arrows together to seal their alliance.

sentences.zh: 按陳曰：「吾還奏，當以征遼之責屬爾。」

translations.literal: Anchanna said: "When I return and report, the responsibility of campaigning against Liao shall be entrusted to you."
translations.idiomatic: Anchanna said: "When I return to report, I shall assign you the task of conquering Liao."

sentences.zh: 金人遣胡沙帥軍六十萬，號百萬，來攻留哥，聲言有得留哥骨一兩者，賞金一兩，肉一兩者，賞銀亦如之，仍世襲千戶。

translations.literal: The Jurchens sent Husha at the head of six hundred thousand troops—they claimed a million—to attack Liuge. They proclaimed that one tael of weight in Liuge's bones would earn a reward of one tael of gold, and one tael of his flesh the same weight in silver; they also promised hereditary chiliarch rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin sent Husha with six hundred thousand troops—proclaimed as a million—to attack Liuge. They offered one tael of gold for each tael of his bones and one tael of silver for each tael of his flesh, with the rank of chiliarch made hereditary to whoever brought them in.

sentences.zh: 留哥度不能敵，亟馳表聞。

translations.literal: Liuge judged that he could not resist, and urgently dispatched a memorial to report.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he could not hold them off, Liuge sent an urgent dispatch to the Khan.

sentences.zh: 帝命按陳、孛都歡、阿魯都罕引千騎會留哥，與金兵對陣于迪吉腦兒。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Anchanna, Beduhuan, and Arudukan to lead a thousand riders to join Liuge, and they drew up against the Jin army at Dijinao'er.
translations.idiomatic: The Khan ordered Anchanna, Beduhuan, and Arudukan to lead a thousand horsemen to Liuge's aid. They confronted the Jin army at Dijinao'er.

sentences.zh: 留哥以姪安奴為先鋒，橫衝胡沙軍，大敗之，以所俘輜重獻。

translations.literal: Liuge made his nephew Annu vanguard; he charged across Husha's army and routed it utterly, presenting the captured baggage train in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Liuge sent his nephew Annu as vanguard in a sweeping charge against Husha's forces and won a great victory. He presented the captured baggage train to the Khan.

sentences.zh: 帝召按陳還，而以可特哥副留哥屯其地。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Anchanna back and left Ketige to assist Liuge in garrisoning the region.
translations.idiomatic: The Khan recalled Anchanna and left Ketige as Liuge's deputy to hold the territory.

sentences.zh: 衆以遼東未定，癸酉三月，推留哥為王，立妻姚里氏為妃，以其屬耶冢不為郡王，坡沙、僧家奴、耶的、李家奴等為丞相、元帥、尚書，統古與、著撥行元帥府事，國號遼。

translations.literal: Because Liaodong was not yet settled, in the third month of the guiyou year the multitude made Liuge king, installed his wife Yelü Yelishi as consort, appointed his followers Yelü Zhongbu as prince of a commandery, Posa, Sengjianu, Yede, Li Jianu, and others as chancellor, commander, and secretary, with Tongguyu and Zhubo administering the supreme commandery headquarters, and took Liao as the state name.
translations.idiomatic: With Liaodong still unsettled, in the third month of guiyou (1213) his followers proclaimed Liuge king. They made his wife Yelü Yelishi his consort, appointed Yelü Zhongbu and others as princes and ministers, set Tongguyu and Zhuobo over the military headquarters, and revived the state name of Liao.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，金遣使青狗誘以重祿使降，不從。

translations.literal: In the jiaxu year, the Jin sent the envoy Qinggou to entice him with rich rewards to surrender; he would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: In jiaxu (1214), the Jin sent an envoy named Qinggou, offering lavish rewards if Liuge would surrender. He refused.

sentences.zh: 青狗度其勢不可，反臣之。

translations.literal: Qinggou judged that the situation could not be turned, and instead submitted to Liuge as a minister.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Liuge's position could not be overcome, Qinggou turned about and submitted to him instead.

sentences.zh: 金主怒，復遣宣撫萬奴領軍四十餘萬攻之。

translations.literal: The Jin ruler was enraged and again sent the pacification commissioner Wannu at the head of more than four hundred thousand troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor, furious, sent the pacification commissioner Wannu with over four hundred thousand troops against him.

sentences.zh: 留哥逆戰于歸仁縣北河上，金兵大潰，萬奴收散卒奔東京。

translations.literal: Liuge met them in battle on the river north of Guiren County; the Jin army was utterly routed, and Wannu gathered the scattered troops and fled to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Liuge met them on the river north of Guiren County and won a crushing victory. Wannu gathered what remained of his army and fled to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 安東同知阿憐懼，遣使求附。

translations.literal: Alian, the associate administrator of Andong, was afraid and sent envoys to seek submission.
translations.idiomatic: Alian, deputy administrator of Andong, was terrified and sent envoys to offer his allegiance.

sentences.zh: 於是盡有遼東州郡，遂都咸平，號為中京。

translations.literal: Thereupon he possessed all the prefectures and districts of Liaodong, made Xianping his capital, and styled it the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He now held all the prefectures of Liaodong. He made Xianping his capital and styled it the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 金左副元帥移剌都，以兵十萬攻留哥，拒戰，敗之。

translations.literal: Yelü Du, the Jin's left deputy commander, attacked Liuge with a hundred thousand troops; Liuge resisted in battle and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Du, the Jin's left deputy commander, attacked with a hundred thousand men. Liuge met him in battle and routed his army.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，留哥破東京，可特哥娶萬奴之妻李僊娥，留哥不直之，有隙。

translations.literal: In the yihai year, Liuge captured the Eastern Capital. Ketige took Wannu's wife Li Xian'e as his own; Liuge disapproved, and a rift arose between them.
translations.idiomatic: In yihai (1215), Liuge captured the Eastern Capital. Ketige took Wannu's wife Li Xian'e for himself—a deed Liuge condemned, and ill feeling grew between them.

sentences.zh: 既而耶冢不等勸留哥稱帝，留哥曰：「向者吾與按陳那衍盟，願附大蒙古國，削平疆宇。

translations.literal: Before long Yelü Zhongbu and others urged Liuge to declare himself emperor. Liuge said: "Formerly I covenanted with Anchanna, wishing to attach myself to the Great Mongol State and level all territories.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yelü Zhongbu and others urged Liuge to take the imperial title. Liuge said: "I once swore an alliance with Anchanna, pledging to submit to the Great Mongol State and help conquer the realm.

sentences.zh: 倘食其言而自為東帝，是逆天也，逆天者必有大咎。」

translations.literal: If I now eat my words and make myself emperor of the east, that would be defying Heaven; whoever defies Heaven will surely suffer great calamity."
translations.idiomatic: If I break that pledge now and proclaim myself emperor of the east, I would be defying Heaven—and those who defy Heaven bring great disaster upon themselves."

sentences.zh: 衆請愈力，不獲已，稱疾不出。

translations.literal: The crowd pressed their request ever more urgently; unable to refuse outright, he pleaded illness and would not appear.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed him all the harder, but he would not yield. At last he pleaded illness and refused to come forth.

sentences.zh: 潛與其子薛闍奉金幣九十車、金銀牌五百，至按坦孛都罕入覲。

translations.literal: Secretly he and his son Xieshe brought ninety cartloads of gold coins and five hundred gold and silver plaques to Altan Beduhan to present themselves in audience.
translations.idiomatic: In secret he sent his son Xieshe with ninety cartloads of gold and five hundred gold and silver plaques to Altan Beduhan, and went to present himself at court.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「漢人先納款者，先引見。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Among the Han who first submitted, let the first be brought in audience first."
translations.idiomatic: The Khan said: "Among the Han who submitted first, let the first-comer be received first."

sentences.zh: 太傅阿海奏曰：「劉伯林納款最先。」

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Ahai memorialized: "Liu Bolin submitted first."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Ahai reported: "Liu Bolin was the first to submit."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「伯林雖先，然迫於重圍而來，未若留哥仗義效順也，其先留哥。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Although Bolin came first, he came under the pressure of heavy siege; he is not like Liuge, who acted from righteousness in submitting. Let Liuge come first."
translations.idiomatic: The Khan said: "Bolin may have come first, but he came only because he was hard pressed in siege. Liuge submitted out of principle. Let Liuge be received first."

sentences.zh: 既見，帝大悅，謂左右曰：「凡留哥所獻，白之於天，乃可受。」

translations.literal: After the audience the Emperor was greatly pleased and said to those beside him: "Whatever Liuge offers must be declared to Heaven before it may be accepted."
translations.idiomatic: After receiving him, the Khan was greatly pleased and told his attendants: "Whatever Liuge presents must be offered to Heaven before we may accept it."

sentences.zh: 遂以白氊陳於前，七日而後納諸庫。

translations.literal: Thereupon white felt was spread before him; only after seven days were the gifts placed in the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: White felt was spread before the gifts, and only after seven days were they placed in the treasury.

sentences.zh: 因問舊何官，對曰：「遼王。」

translations.literal: He then asked what office he had formerly held. Liuge answered: "King of Liao."
translations.idiomatic: The Khan asked what rank he had held before. Liuge answered: "King of Liao."

sentences.zh: 帝命賜金虎符，仍遼王。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered that a gold tiger tally be bestowed on him, and that he remain King of Liao.
translations.idiomatic: The Khan ordered a gold tiger tally bestowed on him and confirmed him as King of Liao.

sentences.zh: 又間戶籍幾何，對曰：「六十餘萬。」

translations.literal: He further asked how many registered households he had. Liuge answered: "More than six hundred thousand."
translations.idiomatic: He asked how many households were under his rule. Liuge answered: "More than six hundred thousand."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「可發三千人為質，朕遣蒙古三百人往取之，汝亦遣人偕往。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "You may send three thousand men as hostages. I shall dispatch three hundred Mongols to fetch them; you too shall send men to go together."
translations.idiomatic: The Khan said: "Send three thousand men as hostages. I will send three hundred Mongols to escort them back—you must send men to go with them."

sentences.zh: 留哥遣大夫乞奴、安撫禿哥與俱。

translations.literal: Liuge sent the grandee Qinu and the pacification commissioner Tuge to go with them.
translations.idiomatic: Liuge sent the grandee Qinu and the pacification commissioner Tuge to accompany them.

sentences.zh: 且命詰可特哥曰：「爾妻萬奴之妻，悖法尤甚。」

translations.literal: He also ordered that Ketige be questioned, saying: "Your taking Wannu's wife as your own is a grave violation of law."
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Ketige summoned and rebuked: "You took Wannu's wife for yourself—a grave breach of law."

sentences.zh: 其拘縶以來。

translations.literal: He was to be seized and brought in.
translations.idiomatic: He was to be seized and brought back.

sentences.zh: 可特哥懼，與耶冢不等紿其衆曰：「留哥已死。」

translations.literal: Ketige was afraid; he and Yelü Zhongbu and others deceived their troops, saying: "Liuge is already dead."
translations.idiomatic: Ketige was terrified. He and Yelü Zhongbu and others deceived their troops, claiming that Liuge was dead.

sentences.zh: 遂以其衆叛，殺所遣三百人，惟三人逃歸。

translations.literal: Thereupon they rebelled with their forces, killed the three hundred men who had been sent, and only three escaped back.
translations.idiomatic: They then rebelled with their forces, killed the three hundred Mongols who had been sent, and only three men escaped to report back.

sentences.zh: 事聞，帝諭留哥曰：「爾毋以失衆為憂，朕倍此數封汝無吝也。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the Emperor told Liuge: "Do not grieve over the loss of your followers; I shall double this number in enfeoffing you and will not be stingy.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the Khan, he told Liuge: "Do not grieve over the loss of your followers. I shall double your grant in rank and territory—be assured of that.

sentences.zh: 草青馬肥，資爾甲兵，往取家孥。」

translations.literal: When the grass is green and the horses fat, I shall supply you with armor and weapons—go and recover your wives and children."
translations.idiomatic: When the grass turns green and the horses grow fat, I will arm you—go and recover your family."

sentences.zh: 丙子，乞奴、金山、青狗、統古與等推耶冢不僭帝號於澄州，國號遼，改元天威，以留哥兄獨剌為平章，置百官。

translations.literal: In the bingzi year, Qinu, Jinshan, Qinggou, Tongguyu, and others made Yelü Zhongbu usurp the imperial title at Chengzhou, took Liao as the state name, changed the era name to Tianwei, appointed Liuge's elder brother Dula as chief minister, and established the full bureaucracy.
translations.idiomatic: In bingzi (1216), Qinu, Jinshan, Qinggou, Tongguyu, and others proclaimed Yelü Zhongbu emperor at Chengzhou, revived the state name Liao, adopted the era name Tianwei, made Liuge's elder brother Dula chief minister, and set up a full court.

sentences.zh: 方閱月，其元帥青狗叛歸于金，耶冢不為其下所殺，推其丞相乞奴監國，與其行元帥鴉兒，分兵民為左右翼，屯開、保州關。

translations.literal: Barely a month had passed when their commander Qinggou rebelled and returned to the Jin; Yelü Zhongbu was killed by his subordinates. They made his chancellor Qinu regent of the state, and together with the campaigning commander Ya'er divided troops and people into left and right wings, encamping at the passes of Kai and Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month their commander Qinggou defected back to the Jin, and Yelü Zhongbu was killed by his own men. They made his chancellor Qinu regent and, with the campaigning commander Ya'er, divided their forces into left and right wings and encamped at the Kai and Bao passes.

sentences.zh: 金蓋州守將衆家奴引兵攻敗之。

translations.literal: Zhongjianu, the Jin garrison commander of Gaizhou, led troops in attack and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjianu, the Jin commander defending Gaizhou, led troops against them and routed their army.

sentences.zh: 留哥引蒙古軍數千適至，得兄獨剌并妻姚里氏，戶二千。

translations.literal: Liuge arrived just then leading several thousand Mongol troops, recovered his elder brother Dula together with his wife Yelü Yelishi, and two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Liuge arrived just then with several thousand Mongol troops. He recovered his elder brother Dula and his wife Yelü Yelishi, along with two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 鴉兒引敗軍東走，留哥追擊之，還度遼河，招撫懿州、廣寧，徙居臨潢府。

translations.literal: Ya'er led the defeated army east in flight; Liuge pursued and struck them, then recrossed the Liao River, pacified Yizhou and Guangning, and moved his residence to Linhuang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ya'er fled east with the remnants of his army. Liuge pursued, then recrossed the Liao River, pacified Yizhou and Guangning, and moved his seat to Linhuang.

sentences.zh: 乞奴走高麗，為金山所殺，金山又自稱國王，改元天德。

translations.literal: Qinu fled to Goryeo and was killed by Jinshan; Jinshan then declared himself king and changed the era name to Tiande.
translations.idiomatic: Qinu fled to Goryeo, where Jinshan killed him. Jinshan then proclaimed himself king and adopted the era name Tiande.

sentences.zh: 統古與復殺金山而自立，喊舍又殺之，亦自立。

translations.literal: Tongguyu again killed Jinshan and set himself up; Hanshe then killed him and likewise declared himself ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Tongguyu killed Jinshan and seized power in turn; Hanshe then killed Tongguyu and proclaimed himself ruler as well.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，留哥引蒙古、契丹軍及東夏國元帥胡土兵十萬，圍喊舍。

translations.literal: In the wuyin year, Liuge led Mongol and Khitan troops together with the Eastern Xia state commander Hutu and a hundred thousand soldiers to besiege Hanshe.
translations.idiomatic: In wuyin (1218), Liuge led Mongol and Khitan troops, together with the Eastern Xia commander Hutu and a hundred thousand men, to besiege Hanshe.

sentences.zh: 高麗助兵四十萬，克之，喊舍自經死。

translations.literal: Goryeo sent four hundred thousand troops in aid; they captured the place, and Hanshe hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo sent four hundred thousand reinforcements. They took the stronghold, and Hanshe hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 徙其民於西樓。

translations.literal: His people were relocated to Xilou.
translations.idiomatic: His people were resettled at Xilou.

sentences.zh: 自乙亥歲留哥北覲，遼東反覆，耶冢不僭號七十餘日，金山二年，統古與、喊舍亦近二年，至己卯春，留哥復定之。

translations.literal: From the yihai year when Liuge went north to audience, Liaodong was in turmoil: Yelü Zhongbu usurped the title for more than seventy days; Jinshan for two years; Tongguyu and Hanshe for nearly two years as well—until the spring of the jimao year, when Liuge pacified it again.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Liuge went north to court in yihai (1215), Liaodong was in constant upheaval: Yelü Zhongbu held the title for over seventy days, Jinshan for two years, Tongguyu and Hanshe for nearly two years each—until the spring of jimao (1219), when Liuge restored order.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，留哥卒，年五十六。

translations.literal: In the gengchen year, Liuge died, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In gengchen (1220), Liuge died at the age of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 妻姚里氏入奏，會帝征西域，皇太弟承制以姚里氏佩虎符，權領其衆者七年。

translations.literal: His wife Yelü Yelishi presented a memorial at court. It happened that the Emperor was campaigning in the Western Regions; the Imperial Younger Brother, acting under delegated authority, had Yelü Yelishi wear the tiger tally and exercise command over his followers for seven years.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Yelü Yelishi reported to court. The Khan was away campaigning in the west, and the Imperial Younger Brother, acting with delegated authority, had her wear the tiger tally and command Liuge's followers for seven years.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，帝還，姚里氏攜次子善哥、鐵哥、永安及從子塔塔兒，孫收國奴，見帝于河西阿里湫城。

translations.literal: In the bingxu year the Emperor returned; Yelü Yelishi brought her second sons Shange, Tiege, and Yong'an, her nephew Tatat'er, and her grandson Shouguonu to audience with the Emperor at Aliqiu city in Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In bingxu (1226) the Khan returned from the west. Yelü Yelishi brought her younger sons Shange, Tiege, and Yong'an, her nephew Tatat'er, and her grandson Shouguonu to meet him at Aliqiu in Hexi.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「健鷹飛不到之地，爾婦人乃能來耶！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "This is a place no strong eagle can reach—yet you, a woman, have been able to come!"
translations.idiomatic: The Khan said: "This is country no strong eagle can reach—yet you, a woman, have made the journey!"

sentences.zh: 賜之酒，慰勞甚至。

translations.literal: He bestowed wine on her and comforted her with exceptional kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He gave her wine and comforted her with exceptional warmth.

sentences.zh: 姚里氏奏曰：「留哥既沒，官民乏主，其長子薛闍扈從有年，願以次子善哥代之，使歸襲爵。」

translations.literal: Yelü Yelishi memorialized: "Now that Liuge is gone, officials and people lack a lord. His eldest son Xieshe has attended Your Majesty for many years; I wish to have the second son Shange replace him in attendance, so that Xieshe may return to inherit the title."
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Yelishi petitioned: "Since Liuge's death, his officials and people have lacked a leader. His eldest son Xieshe has served at your side for years. I ask that his second son Shange take his place in attendance, so that Xieshe may return home to inherit his father's rank."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「薛闍今為蒙古人矣，其從朕之征西域也，回回圍太子於合迷城，薛闍引千軍救出之，身中槊；

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Xieshe is now a Mongol. When he followed me in the campaign against the Western Regions, the Muslims besieged the Crown Prince at Hemi city; Xieshe led a thousand troops to rescue him and was struck by a spear;
translations.idiomatic: The Khan said: "Xieshe is a Mongol now. On our western campaign, when Muslims besieged the Crown Prince at Hemi, Xieshe led a thousand men to rescue him and took a spear wound;

sentences.zh: 又於蒲華、尋思干城與回回格戰，傷於流矢。

translations.literal: again at Puhua and Xunsi'gan cities he fought the Muslims in close combat and was wounded by a stray arrow.
translations.idiomatic: at Puhua and Xunsi'gan he fought the Muslims hand to hand and was wounded by a stray arrow.

sentences.zh: 以是積功為拔都魯，不可遣，當令善哥襲其父爵。」

translations.literal: For these accumulated merits he was made a baturu; he cannot be sent away. Shange should inherit his father's title."
translations.idiomatic: For these deeds he was made a baturu. He cannot be spared. Let Shange inherit his father's title instead."

sentences.zh: 姚里氏拜且泣曰：「薛闍者，留哥前妻所出，嫡子也，宜立。

translations.literal: Yelü Yelishi bowed and wept, saying: "Xieshe was born of Liuge's former wife; he is the legitimate son and ought to be established.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Yelishi bowed and wept. "Xieshe was born of Liuge's first wife—the legitimate heir. He should succeed.

sentences.zh: 善哥者，婢子所出，若立之，是私己而蔑天倫，婢子竊以為不可。」

translations.literal: Shange was born of a servant girl; to establish him would be favoring myself and scorning the bonds of kinship. Your servant humbly thinks this cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Shange was born of a servant girl. To install him would be to favor my own child and violate the bonds of kinship. I humbly believe that cannot be right."

sentences.zh: 帝嘆其賢，給驛騎四十，從征河西，賜河西俘人九口、馬九匹、白金九錠，幣器皆以九計，許以薛闍襲爵，而留善哥、塔塔兒、收國奴於朝，惟遣其季子永安從姚里氏東歸。

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed at her virtue, gave her forty relay horses to follow the Hexi campaign, bestowed nine Hexi captives, nine horses, and nine ingots of white metal, with all silks and vessels counted in nines, permitted Xieshe to inherit the title, but kept Shange, Tatat'er, and Shouguonu at court, sending only her youngest son Yong'an east with Yelü Yelishi.
translations.idiomatic: The Khan marveled at her integrity. He gave her forty relay horses for the Hexi campaign and bestowed nine captives, nine horses, nine ingots of silver, and gifts of silk and vessels—all in counts of nine. He allowed Xieshe to inherit the title but kept Shange, Tatat'er, and Shouguonu at court, sending only her youngest son Yong'an east with her.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，帝召薛闍謂曰：「昔女真猖獗，爾父起兵，自遼東會朕師，又能割愛，以爾事朕，其情貞愨可尚。

translations.literal: In the dinghai year the Emperor summoned Xieshe and said: "Formerly the Jurchens ran rampant; your father raised troops and joined my army from Liaodong, and could moreover part with his beloved son and give you to serve me—such steadfast loyalty is admirable.
translations.idiomatic: In dinghai (1227) the Khan summoned Xieshe and said: "When the Jurchens were at their height, your father raised troops in Liaodong and joined my army. He could even part with his beloved son and give you to serve me—that steadfast loyalty is admirable.

sentences.zh: 繼而奸人耶冢不等叛，人民離散。

translations.literal: Afterward the traitors Yelü Zhongbu and others rebelled, and the people were scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Then traitors like Yelü Zhongbu rebelled, and his people were scattered.

sentences.zh: 欲食爾父子之肉者，今豈無人乎！

translations.literal: Those who wished to eat the flesh of you father and son—are there none such even now!
translations.idiomatic: Those who would have devoured you and your father—do you think they are all gone?

sentences.zh: 朕以兄弟視爾父，則爾猶吾子，爾父亡矣，爾其與吾弟孛魯古台並轄軍馬，為第三千戶。」

translations.literal: I regarded your father as a brother, so you are as my son. Your father is gone; you shall jointly command troops and horses with my younger brother Belguqutai as the third chiliarch."
translations.idiomatic: I treated your father as a brother, so you are as a son to me. Your father is gone. You shall command troops jointly with my brother Belguqutai as the third chiliarch."

sentences.zh: 薛闍受命。

translations.literal: Xieshe received the command.
translations.idiomatic: Xieshe accepted the appointment.

sentences.zh: 己丑，從太宗南征，有功，賜馬四百、牛六百、羊二百。

translations.literal: In the jichou year he followed Taizong on the southern campaign, performed merit, and was granted four hundred horses, six hundred cattle, and two hundred sheep.
translations.idiomatic: In jichou (1229) he followed Ögedei on the southern campaign, distinguished himself, and was rewarded with four hundred horses, six hundred cattle, and two hundred sheep.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，帝命與撒兒台東征，收其父遺民，移鎮廣寧府，行廣寧路都元帥府事。

translations.literal: In the gengyin year the Emperor ordered him to campaign east with Sa'ertai, recover his father's surviving people, transfer his garrison to Guangning Prefecture, and administer the supreme commandery headquarters of the Guangning circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In gengyin (1230) the Khan ordered him to campaign east with Sa'ertai, recover his father's former subjects, move his headquarters to Guangning, and serve as supreme commander of the Guangning circuit.

sentences.zh: 自庚寅至丁酉，連征高麗、東夏萬奴國，復戶六千有奇。

translations.literal: From gengyin to dingyou he campaigned repeatedly against Goryeo and the Eastern Xia state of Wannu, recovering more than six thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: From gengyin to dingyou (1230–1237) he campaigned repeatedly against Goryeo and the Eastern Xia kingdom of Wannu, recovering more than six thousand households.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，薛闍卒，年四十六。

translations.literal: In the wuxu year Xieshe died, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In wuxu (1238) Xieshe died at the age of forty-six.

sentences.zh: 子收國奴襲爵，行廣寧府路緫管軍民萬戶府事，易名石剌，征高麗，有功。

translations.literal: His son Shouguonu inherited the title, administered the Guangning circuit office of the commander-in-chief over military and civil affairs for the ten-thousand-household unit, changed his name to Shila, campaigned against Goryeo, and performed merit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shouguonu inherited the title and administered the Guangning military-civil headquarters. He took the name Shila, campaigned against Goryeo, and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，睿宗以石剌為國宣力者三代，命益金更造所佩虎符賜之，佐諸王也苦及扎剌台控制高麗。

translations.literal: In the xinhai year Ruizong, because Shila's family had served the state with distinction for three generations, ordered that his gold tiger tally be recast and bestowed anew, and assigned him to assist the princes Yeku and Jalatai in controlling Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In xinhai (1251) Ruizong, noting that Shila's family had served the state with distinction for three generations, ordered his gold tiger tally recast and bestowed anew, and assigned him to assist Princes Yeku and Jalatai in controlling Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 己未卒，年四十五。

translations.literal: In the jiwei year he died, aged forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In jiwei (1259) he died at the age of forty-five.

sentences.zh: 長子古乃嗣。

translations.literal: His eldest son Gunai succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Gunai succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，征河西；

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong he campaigned in Hexi;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong (1260) he campaigned in Hexi;

sentences.zh: 三年，征李璮，破嶧山：以功皆受賞。

translations.literal: in the third year he campaigned against Li Tan and captured Yishan; for these merits he received rewards in each case.
translations.idiomatic: in the third year (1262) he campaigned against Li Tan and took Yishan—for these deeds he was rewarded each time.

sentences.zh: 至元六年，朝廷併廣寧于東京，去職，是歲卒，年三十六。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan the court merged Guangning into the Eastern Capital; he left office, and in that same year died, aged thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan (1269) the court merged Guangning into the Eastern Capital circuit. He left office and died that same year, aged thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 子忒哥。

translations.literal: His son was Teghe.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Teghe.

sentences.zh: 劉伯林

translations.literal: Liu Bolin
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bolin

sentences.zh: 劉伯林，濟南人。

translations.literal: Liu Bolin was a native of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bolin was a native of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 好任俠，善騎射，金末為威寧防城千戶。

translations.literal: He loved bold chivalry and excelled at mounted archery; at the end of the Jin he served as chiliarch for the defense of Weining.
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of chivalrous adventure and skilled in mounted archery. At the end of the Jin dynasty he served as chiliarch defending Weining.

sentences.zh: 壬申歲，太祖圍威寧，伯林知不能敵，乃縋城詣軍門請降。

translations.literal: In the renshen year the Taizu besieged Weining; Bolin knew he could not resist, and so was lowered from the wall to go to the army gate and request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the renshen year (1212) Genghis Khan besieged Weining. Bolin saw he could not hold out and was lowered from the wall to present himself at the camp and offer surrender.

sentences.zh: 太祖許之，遣禿魯花等與偕入城，遂以城降。

translations.literal: The Taizu granted it, sent Tulughua and others to enter the city with him, and the city surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The Khan accepted. He sent Tulughua and others to enter the city with Bolin, and the city surrendered.

sentences.zh: 帝問伯林，在金國為何官，對曰：「都提控。」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Bolin what office he had held in the Jin state. He answered: "Chief commander."
translations.idiomatic: The Khan asked what rank Bolin had held under the Jin. He answered: "Chief commander."

sentences.zh: 即以元職授之，命選士卒為一軍，與太傅耶律禿懷同征討，招降山後諸州。

translations.literal: He was immediately given his former office, ordered to select troops to form an army, and together with Grand Tutor Yelü Tuhuai conducted campaigns to bring the prefectures beyond the mountains to submission.
translations.idiomatic: The Khan confirmed him in his former rank, ordered him to raise an army from selected troops, and sent him with Grand Tutor Yelü Tuhuai to campaign and bring the prefectures north of the Yan Mountains to submission.

sentences.zh: 太祖北還，留伯林屯天成，遏金兵，前後數十戰。

translations.literal: When the Taizu returned north, Bolin was left to garrison Tiancheng, blocking Jin troops in several dozen battles before and after.
translations.idiomatic: When Genghis Khan returned north, Bolin was left to garrison Tiancheng and hold the Jin forces at bay, fighting several dozen engagements.

sentences.zh: 進攻西京，錄功，賜金虎符，以本職充西京留守，兼兵馬副元帥。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack the Western Capital, his merit was recorded; he was granted a gold tiger tally, appointed to his former office as garrison commander of the Western Capital, and concurrently made deputy commander of troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the advance on the Western Capital his merit was recorded. He received a gold tiger tally and was appointed garrison commander of the Western Capital with his former rank, concurrently serving as deputy commander of troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，從征山東，攻梁門、遂城，下之。

translations.literal: In the guiyou year he followed the campaign into Shandong, attacked Liangmen and Suicheng, and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: In guiyou (1213) he joined the Shandong campaign, attacked Liangmen and Suicheng, and took both.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，同國王木華黎攻破燕京。

translations.literal: In the yihai year he joined King Muqali in capturing Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In yihai (1215) he joined Prince Muqali in the capture of Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，復從大軍攻下山東諸州。

translations.literal: In the dingchou year he again followed the main army in reducing the prefectures of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In dingchou (1217) he again followed the main army in reducing the Shandong prefectures.

sentences.zh: 木華黎上其功，賜名馬二十匹、錦衣一襲。

translations.literal: Muqali reported his merit, and he was granted twenty famous horses and one suit of brocade robes.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali reported his achievements, and he was rewarded with twenty fine horses and a brocade robe.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，同攻下太原、平陽。

translations.literal: In the wuyin year he jointly attacked and captured Taiyuan and Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In wuyin (1218) he joined in the capture of Taiyuan and Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 己卯，破潞、絳及火山、聞喜諸州縣。

translations.literal: In the jimao year he captured Lu, Jiang, and the prefectures and districts of Huoshan and Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: In jimao (1219) he captured Lu, Jiang, and the prefectures of Huoshan and Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 時論欲徙聞喜民實天成，伯林以北地喪亂，人艱於食，力爭而止之。

translations.literal: At the time opinion favored relocating the people of Wenxi to populate Tiancheng; Bolin argued strenuously against it because the northern lands were ravaged by disorder and people found food hard to obtain, and the plan was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed resettling Wenxi's people to populate Tiancheng. Bolin argued forcefully that the north was devastated and food scarce, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 部曲所獲俘虜萬計，悉縱之。

translations.literal: Captives taken by his retainers numbered in the tens of thousands; he released them all.
translations.idiomatic: His troops had taken tens of thousands of captives; he released them all.

sentences.zh: 在威寧十餘年，務農積穀，與民休息，鄰境凋瘵，而威寧獨為樂土。

translations.literal: During more than ten years at Weining he devoted himself to farming and storing grain, gave the people rest, and while neighboring territories were wasted and sickly, Weining alone became a land of peace.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years at Weining he promoted farming and grain storage and let the people recover. While neighboring regions lay wasted, Weining alone became a haven.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「吾聞活千人者後必封，吾之所活，何啻萬餘人，子孫必有興者乎！」

translations.literal: He once said: "I have heard that one who keeps a thousand alive will afterward surely be enfeoffed; those I have kept alive are no less than ten thousand and more—surely my descendants will rise!"
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "They say whoever saves a thousand lives will be ennobled. I have saved more than ten thousand—surely my line will prosper!"

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以疾卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the xinsi year he died of illness, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In xinsi (1221) he died of illness at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 累贈太師，封秦國公，諡忠順。

translations.literal: He was posthumously promoted to Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed as Duke of Qin, and given the posthumous title Zhongshun.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed as Duke of Qin, and given the posthumous name Zhongshun, "Loyal and Obedient."

sentences.zh: 子黑馬。

translations.literal: His son was Heima.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Heima.

sentences.zh: 子黑馬

translations.literal: His son Heima
translations.idiomatic: His son Heima

sentences.zh: 黑馬名嶷，字孟方，始生時，家有白馬產黑駒，故以為小字，後遂以小字行。

translations.literal: Heima's given name was Ni, courtesy name Mengfang. At his birth the household had a white horse that foaled a black colt, so this became his informal name, and afterward he was known by that informal name.
translations.idiomatic: Heima's given name was Ni, courtesy name Mengfang. At his birth the family white mare foaled a black colt, which became his childhood name; he was known by it ever after.

sentences.zh: 驍勇有志略，年幾弱冠，隨父征伐，大小數百戰，出入行陣，略無懼色。

translations.literal: Fierce and brave with strategic resolve, when he was nearly of age he followed his father in campaigns, fighting several hundred engagements large and small, entering and leaving the battle lines with scarcely a sign of fear.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and resourceful, he followed his father into battle before he came of age, fighting hundreds of engagements and showing scarcely a trace of fear in the thick of combat.

sentences.zh: 嘗獨行，遇金兵圍本部十三人，即奮劍入圍，手殺金兵數人，十三人皆得脫。

translations.literal: Once traveling alone, he encountered Jin troops surrounding thirteen men of his command; he immediately brandished his sword and charged into the encirclement, personally killing several Jin soldiers, and all thirteen escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Once, riding alone, he found Jin troops surrounding thirteen of his men. He charged in with drawn sword, killed several Jin soldiers himself, and brought all thirteen out alive.

sentences.zh: 歲壬午，襲父職，為萬戶，佩虎符，兼都元帥。

translations.literal: In the renwu year he inherited his father's office, became a ten-thousand-household commander, wore the tiger tally, and concurrently served as supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: In renwu (1222) he inherited his father's post as commander of ten thousand households, received the tiger tally, and served concurrently as supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 癸未，從國王木華黎攻鳳翔，不克，回屯絳州。

translations.literal: In the guiwei year he followed King Muqali in attacking Fengxiang but could not take it, and returned to encamp at Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In guiwei (1223) he followed Prince Muqali in the attack on Fengxiang. When it failed, they withdrew to garrison Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 又從孛羅攻西夏唐兀。

translations.literal: He again followed Boluo in attacking the Western Xia Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Boluo in campaigning against the Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 甲申，從按真那延攻破東平、大名。

translations.literal: In the jiashen year he followed Anzhen Nayan in capturing Dongping and Daming.
translations.idiomatic: In jiashen (1224) he followed Anzhen Nayan in the capture of Dongping and Daming.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，金降將武僊據真定以叛，從孛羅討之，破真定，武僊遁去。

translations.literal: In the yiyou year the Jin surrendered general Wu Xian seized Zhending in rebellion; he followed Boluo to suppress him, captured Zhending, and Wu Xian fled.
translations.idiomatic: In yiyou (1225) the Jin defector Wu Xian seized Zhending in rebellion. Heima followed Boluo to suppress him, took the city, and Wu Xian fled.

sentences.zh: 金將忽察虎以兵四十萬復取山後諸州，黑馬逆戰隘胡嶺，大破之，斬忽察虎。

translations.literal: The Jin general Huchahu led four hundred thousand troops to recover the prefectures beyond the mountains; Heima met him in battle at Aihuling Pass, routed him utterly, and beheaded Huchahu.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin general Huchahu led four hundred thousand men to retake the northern prefectures. Heima met him at Aihuling Pass, won a crushing victory, and killed Huchahu.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，從破南京，賜綉衣、玉帶。

translations.literal: In the guisi year he followed in the capture of the Southern Capital and was granted embroidered robes and a jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: In guisi (1233) he joined in the capture of the Southern Capital and was rewarded with embroidered robes and a jade belt.

sentences.zh: 甲午，從破蔡州，滅金。

translations.literal: In the jiawu year he followed in the capture of Caizhou and the destruction of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In jiawu (1234) he joined in the capture of Caizhou and the fall of the Jin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 乙未，同都元帥荅海紺卜征西川。

translations.literal: In the yiwei year he joined the supreme commander Dahai Ganbu in campaigning against western Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In yiwei (1235) he joined Supreme Commander Dahai Ganbu in the campaign against western Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，改授都緫管萬戶，統西京、河東、陝西諸軍萬戶，夾谷忙古歹、田雄等並聽節制。

translations.literal: In the xinchou year he was reassigned as commander-in-chief of the ten-thousand-household units, commanding the military households of the Western Capital, Hedong, and Shaanxi circuits; Jiagu Mangudai, Tian Xiong, and others were all placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: In xinchou (1241) he was appointed commander-in-chief over the military households of the Western Capital, Hedong, and Shaanxi, with Jiagu Mangudai, Tian Xiong, and others under his command.

sentences.zh: 入覲，帝慰勞之，賜銀鼠皮三百為直孫衣。

translations.literal: On presenting himself at court the Emperor comforted him and granted three hundred silver-marten pelts to make garments for his direct grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: At court the Khan welcomed him and granted three hundred silver-marten pelts to make garments for his grandsons.

sentences.zh: 尋命巡撫天下，察民利病。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered to tour and pacify the realm, investigating what benefited or harmed the people.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to tour the realm and investigate the people's welfare.

sentences.zh: 應州郭志全反，脅從詿誤者五百餘人，有司議盡戮之，黑馬止誅其為首者數人，餘悉從輕典。

translations.literal: Guo Zhiquan of Yingzhou rebelled; more than five hundred who had been coerced or misled were implicated. The officials proposed executing them all, but Heima put to death only several ringleaders and treated the rest under lenient statutes.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Zhiquan of Yingzhou rebelled, over five hundred coerced followers were implicated. Officials proposed executing them all, but Heima executed only the ringleaders and treated the rest leniently.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，從憲宗至六盤山。

translations.literal: In the guichou year he followed Xianzong to Liupan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In guichou (1253) he accompanied Möngke Khan to Liupan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 商州與宋接境，數為所侵，命黑馬守之，宋人斂兵不敢犯。

translations.literal: Shangzhou bordered Song territory and was repeatedly raided; Heima was ordered to defend it, and the Song drew in their troops and dared not violate it.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhou bordered Song territory and suffered repeated raids. Heima was assigned to defend it, and the Song held their troops back and dared not attack.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，入覲，請立成都以圖全蜀，帝從之。

translations.literal: In the dingsi year he presented himself at court and requested that Chengdu be established as a base to secure all of Shu; the Emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: In dingsi (1257) he came to court and proposed establishing Chengdu as a base to conquer all of Sichuan. The Khan agreed.

sentences.zh: 成都既立，就命管領新舊軍民小大諸務，賜號也可禿立。

translations.literal: Once Chengdu was established, he was immediately ordered to administer all affairs great and small of old and new troops and civilians, and was granted the title Yeketuli.
translations.idiomatic: With Chengdu established, he was placed in charge of all military and civil affairs there and granted the title Yeketuli.

sentences.zh: 黑馬子元振

translations.literal: Heima's son Yuanzhen
translations.idiomatic: Heima's son Yuanzhen

sentences.zh: 元振字仲舉，黑馬長子也。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen, courtesy name Zhongju, was Heima's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen, courtesy name Zhongju, was Heima's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 隨父入蜀，立成都。

translations.literal: He followed his father into Shu and helped establish Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He followed his father into Sichuan and helped establish Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 會商、鄧間有警，命黑馬往鎮商、鄧，以元振攝萬戶，時年方二十。

translations.literal: When there was alarm between Shang and Deng, Heima was ordered to garrison those regions; Yuanzhen was made acting commander of ten thousand households when he was only twenty.
translations.idiomatic: When trouble arose between Shang and Deng, Heima was sent to garrison those regions and left Yuanzhen as acting commander of ten thousand households—he was only twenty.

sentences.zh: 既蒞事，號令嚴明，賞罰不妄，麾下宿將皆敬服之。

translations.literal: Once he took office his orders were strict and clear, rewards and punishments were not given lightly, and the veteran generals under him all respected and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Once in command, his orders were strict and his rewards and punishments fair. Even the veteran generals under him respected him.

sentences.zh: 憲宗伐宋，駐驛釣魚山，以元振與紐鄰為先鋒。

translations.literal: When Xianzong campaigned against Song and halted at Diaoyu Mountain, Yuanzhen and Niulin were made vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Möngke campaigned against Song and encamped at Diaoyu Mountain, Yuanzhen and Niulin were appointed vanguard.

sentences.zh: 宋瀘州主帥俞興，率兵圍瀘州，晝夜急攻，自正月至五月，城幾陷，左右勸元振曰：「事勢如此，宜思變通，整本非吾人，與俱死，無益也。」

translations.literal: The Song commander of Luzhou, Yu Xing, led troops to besiege Luzhou, attacking day and night without pause. From the first month to the fifth the city was nearly lost. Those beside Yuanzhen urged him: "The situation is thus; you should think of expedients. Zhengben is not one of our people—dying with him would be of no use."
translations.idiomatic: The Song commander of Luzhou, Yu Xing, besieged the city with relentless day-and-night assaults. From the first month to the fifth the walls nearly fell. His officers urged him: "The situation is desperate. Zhengben is not one of us—there is no point dying with him."

sentences.zh: 元振曰：「人以誠歸我，既受其降，豈可以急而棄之。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen said: "People have submitted to us in good faith; having accepted their surrender, how can we abandon them in extremity?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen replied: "They submitted to us in good faith. Having accepted their surrender, how can we abandon them now?

sentences.zh: 且瀘之得失，關國家利害，吾有死而已。」

translations.literal: Moreover, whether Luzhou is held or lost concerns the state's vital interests—I have only death to offer."
translations.idiomatic: Whether Luzhou holds or falls concerns the fate of the realm. I am prepared to die here."

sentences.zh: 食將盡，殺所乘馬犒將士，募善游者齎蠟書至成都求援，又權造金銀牌，分賞有功。

translations.literal: When food was nearly gone he slaughtered his own mount to feast the troops, recruited skilled swimmers to carry sealed letters to Chengdu seeking relief, and on his own authority forged gold and silver plaques to reward those who had merit.
translations.idiomatic: When food ran low he killed his own horse to feed the troops, sent swimmers with sealed dispatches to Chengdu for reinforcements, and on his own authority forged gold and silver plaques to reward the meritorious.

sentences.zh: 未幾，援兵至，元振與整出城合擊興兵，大敗之，斬其都統一人，興退走。

translations.literal: Before long relief arrived; Yuanzhen and Zheng sallied forth and jointly struck Yu Xing's army, routing it utterly, beheading one of his commanders, and Xing retreated in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Soon reinforcements arrived. Yuanzhen and Zheng sallied out and routed Yu Xing's army, killing one of his commanders. Xing fled.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，且自陳擅造金銀牌罪，帝嘉其通於權變，賜錦衣一襲、白金五百兩。

translations.literal: When victory was reported he also confessed the offense of forging gold and silver plaques on his own authority; the Emperor praised his grasp of expedient adaptation and granted him one suit of brocade robes and five hundred taels of white metal.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, he also confessed to forging the plaques without authorization. The Khan praised his resourcefulness and rewarded him with a brocade robe and five hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 入朝，又賜黃金五十兩、弓矢、鞍轡。

translations.literal: On presenting himself at court he was further granted fifty taels of gold, bow and arrows, and saddle and bridle.
translations.idiomatic: At court he received a further fifty taels of gold, a bow and arrows, and saddle and bridle.

sentences.zh: 黑馬卒，元振居喪，起授成都軍民經略使。

translations.literal: When Heima died, Yuanzhen was in mourning but was summoned and appointed commissioner for the military and civil administration of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: When Heima died, Yuanzhen was recalled from mourning and appointed commissioner for the military and civil administration of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 至元七年，時議以勳舊之家事權太重，宜稍裁抑，遂降為成都副萬戶。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan opinion held that meritorious old families wielded too much power and should be somewhat curtailed; he was therefore reduced to deputy commander of ten thousand households at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan (1270), court opinion held that old military families wielded too much power. Yuanzhen was reduced to deputy commander of ten thousand households at Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 十一年，命兼潼川路副招討使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was ordered to serve concurrently as deputy pacification commissioner of the Tongchuan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (1274) he was appointed deputy pacification commissioner of the Tongchuan circuit as well.

sentences.zh: 十二年卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year (1275) he died at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 子緯，數從父行軍。

translations.literal: His son Wei had repeatedly followed his father on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wei had often accompanied his father on campaign.

sentences.zh: 元振卒，緯襲職，佩虎符，為萬戶。

translations.literal: When Yuanzhen died, Wei inherited the office, wore the tiger tally, and became commander of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanzhen died, Wei inherited his post, received the tiger tally, and became commander of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 守潼川，創立遂寧諸處山寨。

translations.literal: He defended Tongchuan and established stockaded strongholds at Suining and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: He defended Tongchuan and established fortified stockades at Suining and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 從圍釣魚山，數戰有功。

translations.literal: He joined the siege of Diaoyu Mountain and performed merit in repeated battles.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the siege of Diaoyu Mountain and distinguished himself in repeated engagements.

sentences.zh: 攻合州，授潼川路副招討，遷副都元帥，復授管軍萬戶，遷同知四川西道宣慰司事。

translations.literal: In the attack on Hezhou he was appointed deputy pacification commissioner of the Tongchuan circuit, promoted to deputy supreme commander, again granted command of military households, and transferred to associate commissioner of the Sichuan Western Circuit Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the attack on Hezhou he was made deputy pacification commissioner of Tongchuan, then deputy supreme commander, then commander of military households, and finally associate commissioner of the Sichuan Western Circuit Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 入朝，進四川西道宣慰使，拜陝西行省參知政事，卒。

translations.literal: On presenting himself at court he was advanced to pacification commissioner of the Sichuan Western Circuit, appointed associate administrator of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, and died.
translations.idiomatic: At court he was promoted to pacification commissioner of the Sichuan Western Circuit and appointed associate administrator of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, then died.

sentences.zh: 元振弟元禮

translations.literal: Yuanzhen's younger brother Yuanli
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen's younger brother Yuanli

sentences.zh: 元禮，黑馬第五子也。

translations.literal: Yuanli was Heima's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli was Heima's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 性沉厚有謀，常從父在軍中。

translations.literal: By nature he was steady and deep, possessed of stratagem, and often followed his father in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Steady and thoughtful by nature, he often accompanied his father on campaign.

sentences.zh: 歲甲寅，授金符，為京兆路奧魯萬戶。

translations.literal: In the jiayin year he was granted a gold tally and appointed commander of the auru of the Jingzhao circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In jiayin (1254) he received a gold tally and was appointed commander of the auru of the Jingzhao circuit.

sentences.zh: 中統四年，遷興元、成都等路兵馬左副元帥。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhongtong he was transferred to left deputy commander of troops and horses for the Xingyuan, Chengdu, and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhongtong (1263) he was made left deputy commander of troops and horses for the Xingyuan and Chengdu circuits.

sentences.zh: 元禮又奏：「嘉定去成都三百六十里，其間舊有眉州城，可修復之，屯兵以扼嘉定往來之路。」

translations.literal: Yuanli further memorialized: "Jiading is three hundred and sixty li from Chengdu. Between them there was formerly the city of Meizhou, which can be restored and garrisoned to choke the route of traffic to and from Jiading."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli further proposed: "Jiading lies three hundred and sixty li from Chengdu. The old city of Meizhou between them could be restored and garrisoned to block traffic to and from Jiading."

sentences.zh: 世祖從之。

translations.literal: Shizu assented.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai Khan agreed.

sentences.zh: 四年，命平章趙寶臣往視可否，或以為眉州荒廢已久，立之無關利害，徒費財力，元禮力爭之，寶臣是其言，遂興役，七日而畢，宋人駭其速。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he ordered the chief minister Zhao Baochen to inspect whether it was feasible. Some held that Meizhou had lain waste for long and that establishing it was of no strategic consequence, merely wasting resources; Yuanli argued forcefully, Baochen endorsed his view, and the work was undertaken and completed in seven days, astonishing the Song with its speed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the chief minister Zhao Baochen was sent to assess the plan. Some argued that Meizhou had been abandoned too long to matter. Yuanli argued forcefully; Baochen agreed, and the work was completed in seven days, astonishing the Song.

sentences.zh: 元禮鎮守眉州五年，召入朝，乞解官養母，從之。

translations.literal: Yuanli garrisoned Meizhou for five years, was summoned to court, and requested to resign office to care for his mother; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli garrisoned Meizhou for five years, then was summoned to court and asked to resign to care for his mother. His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 九年，起授懷遠大將軍、延安路緫管，卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was recalled and appointed General of Far-Reaching Might and administrator of the Yan'an circuit, then died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1272) he was recalled as General of Far-Reaching Might and administrator of the Yan'an circuit, then died.

sentences.zh: 郭寶玉

translations.literal: Guo Baoyu
translations.idiomatic: Guo Baoyu

sentences.zh: 郭寶玉字玉臣，華州鄭縣人，唐中書令子儀之裔也。

translations.literal: Guo Baoyu, courtesy name Yuchen, was a native of Zheng County in Huazhou and a descendant of Guo Ziyi, chief minister of the Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Baoyu, courtesy name Yuchen, was a native of Zheng County in Huazhou and a descendant of the Tang minister Guo Ziyi.

sentences.zh: 通天文、兵法，善騎射。

translations.literal: He was versed in astronomy and military science and excelled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was versed in astronomy and military science and skilled in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 金末，封汾陽郡公，兼猛安，引軍屯定州。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jin he was enfeoffed as Duke of Fenyang, concurrently held a meng'an command, and led troops to garrison Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jin he was enfeoffed as Duke of Fenyang, held a meng'an command, and garrisoned Dingzhou with his troops.

sentences.zh: 歲庚午，童謠曰：「搖搖罟罟，至河南，拜閼氏。」

translations.literal: In the gengwu year a children's rhyme ran: "Yaoyao gugu, reaching Henan, bowing to the Lady."
translations.idiomatic: In gengwu (1210) a children's rhyme ran: "Yaoyao gugu, reaching Henan, bowing to the Lady."

sentences.zh: 既而太白經天，寶玉嘆曰：「北軍南，汴梁即降，天改姓矣。」

translations.literal: Before long Venus crossed the heavens; Baoyu sighed and said: "Northern armies are coming south; Bianliang will soon surrender—the heavens have changed their surname."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Venus crossed the heavens. Baoyu sighed: "Northern armies are coming south. Bianliang will fall—the mandate of heaven has changed hands."

sentences.zh: 金人以獨吉思忠、僕散揆行中書省，領兵築烏沙堡，會太師木華黎軍忽至，敗其兵三十餘萬，思忠等走，寶玉舉軍降。

translations.literal: The Jurchens sent Dugusizhong and Pusan Kui to administer the Branch Secretariat and lead troops to build Wusha Fort. Grand Preceptor Muqali's army suddenly arrived, routed more than three hundred thousand of their troops, and Sizhong and the others fled; Baoyu surrendered his entire army.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin sent Dugusizhong and Pusan Kui to build Wusha Fort. Muqali's army suddenly appeared, routed over three hundred thousand Jin troops, and Sizhong fled. Baoyu surrendered his entire force.

sentences.zh: 木華黎引見太祖，問取中原之策，寶玉對曰：「中原勢大，不可忽也。

translations.literal: Muqali presented him to the Taizu and asked his strategy for taking the Central Plains. Baoyu replied: "The Central Plains are powerful and must not be slighted.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali presented him to Genghis Khan and asked his strategy for conquering China. Baoyu replied: "The Central Plains are powerful and must not be underestimated.

sentences.zh: 西南諸蕃勇悍可用，宜先取之，藉以圖金，必得志焉。」

translations.literal: The southwestern tribes are fierce and can be used; they should be taken first, and by means of them one may plot against Jin—success is certain."
translations.idiomatic: The tribes of the southwest are fierce and useful. Take them first, then use them against the Jin—you will prevail."

sentences.zh: 又言：「建國之初，宜頒新令。」

translations.literal: He also said: "At the founding of the state, new ordinances should be promulgated."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "At the founding of the state, new laws should be promulgated."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The Khan agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是頒條畫五章，如出軍不得妄殺；

translations.literal: Thereupon five articles of regulation were promulgated, such as that troops on campaign must not kill recklessly;
translations.idiomatic: Five articles of law were then promulgated, including that troops on campaign must not kill recklessly;

sentences.zh: 刑獄惟重罪處死，其餘雜犯量情笞決；

translations.literal: in criminal cases only grave offenses were punished by death, while other miscellaneous offenses were punished by flogging according to circumstances;
translations.idiomatic: only capital crimes were punishable by death, while lesser offenses were punished by flogging according to circumstances;

sentences.zh: 軍戶，蒙古、色目人每丁起一軍，漢人有田四頃、人三丁者簽一軍；

translations.literal: for military households, each Mongol or semu man furnished one soldier from each adult male; among Han, those with four qing of land or three adult males in a household furnished one soldier;
translations.idiomatic: for military households, each Mongol or semu adult male furnished one soldier; among Han, one soldier was levied from every household with four qing of land or three adult males;

sentences.zh: 年十五以上成丁，六十破老，站戶與軍戶同；

translations.literal: from age fifteen one became an adult male, at sixty one was released as old; relay households were treated the same as military households;
translations.idiomatic: adulthood began at fifteen and old age at sixty; relay households were treated like military households;

sentences.zh: 民匠限地一頃；

translations.literal: civilian artisans were limited to one qing of land;
translations.idiomatic: civilian artisans were limited to one qing of land;

sentences.zh: 僧道無益於國、有損於民者悉行禁止之類：皆寶玉所陳也。

translations.literal: and Buddhist and Daoist practices that did not benefit the state but harmed the people were all to be prohibited—such were the proposals Baoyu made.
translations.idiomatic: and Buddhist and Daoist practices that harmed the people were to be prohibited—all proposals made by Baoyu.

sentences.zh: 帝將伐西蕃，患其城多依山險，問寶玉攻取之策，對曰：「使其城在天上，則不可取，如不在天上，至則取矣。」

translations.literal: When the Emperor was about to campaign against the western Tibetans and worried that their cities mostly lay in mountainous defiles, he asked Baoyu for a strategy to capture them. He replied: "If their cities were in the sky they could not be taken; if they are not in the sky, when we arrive we shall take them."
translations.idiomatic: When the Khan prepared to campaign against the western Tibetans and worried about their mountain fortresses, he asked Baoyu how to take them. Baoyu replied: "If their cities were in the sky they could not be taken. Since they are not, we shall take them when we arrive."

sentences.zh: 帝壯之，授抄馬都鎮撫。

translations.literal: The Emperor was impressed and appointed him commander of the mounted scouts.
translations.idiomatic: The Khan was impressed and appointed him commander of the mounted scouts.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，從木華黎取永清，破高州，降北京、龍山，復帥抄馬從錦州出燕南，破太原、平陽諸州縣。

translations.literal: In the guiyou year he followed Muqali in taking Yongqing, captured Gaozhou, received the surrender of the Northern Capital and Longshan, again led mounted scouts from Jizhou into southern Yan, and captured Taiyuan, Pingyang, and other prefectures and districts.
translations.idiomatic: In guiyou (1213) he followed Muqali in taking Yongqing, captured Gaozhou, received the surrender of the Northern Capital and Longshan, led scouts from Jizhou into southern Hebei, and captured Taiyuan, Pingyang, and other cities.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，從帝討契丹遺族，歷古徐鬼國訛夷朶等城，破其兵三十餘萬。

translations.literal: In the jiaxu year he followed the Emperor in suppressing the surviving Khitan, passing through the cities of Guxugui, E'yiduo, and others, and routed more than three hundred thousand of their troops.
translations.idiomatic: In jiaxu (1214) he followed the Khan in suppressing the surviving Khitan, passing through Guxugui, E'yiduo, and other cities, and routing over three hundred thousand of their troops.

sentences.zh: 寶玉胸中流矢，帝命剖牛腹置其中，少頃，乃蘇。

translations.literal: Baoyu took a stray arrow in the chest; the Emperor ordered an ox belly slit open and him placed inside, and before long he revived.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu took a stray arrow in the chest. The Khan ordered him placed inside a freshly slaughtered ox, and before long he revived.

sentences.zh: 尋復戰，收別失八里、別失蘭等城。

translations.literal: Soon he fought again and recovered Bieshibali, Bieshilan, and other cities.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned to battle and recovered Bieshibali, Bieshilan, and other cities.

sentences.zh: 次忽章河，西人列兩陣迎拒，戰方酣，寶玉望其衆，疾呼曰：「西陣走矣！」

translations.literal: At the Huzhang River the westerners drew up in two formations to resist; as the battle grew fierce Baoyu looked at their host and cried out: "The western formation is fleeing!"
translations.idiomatic: At the Huzhang River the westerners drew up in two formations to resist. As battle raged, Baoyu looked at their lines and shouted: "The western formation is fleeing!"

sentences.zh: 其兵果走，追殺幾盡。

translations.literal: Their troops indeed fled, and in pursuit nearly all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Their troops indeed fled, and the pursuers killed nearly all of them.

sentences.zh: 進兵下撏思干城。

translations.literal: Advancing, they took the city of Samarkand.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced and took Samarkand.

sentences.zh: 次暗木河，敵築十餘壘，陳船河中，俄風濤暴起，寶玉令發火箭射其船，一時延燒，乘勝直前，破護岸兵五萬，斬大將佐里，遂屠諸壘，收馬里四城。

translations.literal: At the Anmu River the enemy built more than ten stockades and arrayed boats in the river. Suddenly wind and waves rose violently; Baoyu ordered fire-arrows shot at their boats, which burned all at once. Seizing victory they pressed straight forward, broke the shore-guard troops of fifty thousand, beheaded the great general Zuoli, then slaughtered all the stockades and recovered the four cities of Mali.
translations.idiomatic: At the Anmu River the enemy built over ten stockades and lined boats across the river. When wind and waves rose, Baoyu ordered fire-arrows shot at the boats, which burned at once. Pressing the advantage, they broke fifty thousand shore defenders, killed the general Zuoli, destroyed the stockades, and recovered four cities of Mali.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，可弗叉國唯筭端罕破乃滿國，引兵據撏思干，聞帝將至，棄城南走，入鐵門，屯大雪山，寶玉追之，遂奔印度。

translations.literal: In the xinsi year Kefucha Weisuan Duanhan of the Naiman state, having broken the Naiman kingdom, led troops to hold Samarkand. Hearing the Emperor was coming, he abandoned the city and fled south, entered the Iron Gate, and encamped on Great Snow Mountain; Baoyu pursued him, and he fled to India.
translations.idiomatic: In xinsi (1221) Kefucha Weisuan Duanhan of the Naiman, having destroyed the Naiman kingdom, held Samarkand. Hearing the Khan approach, he abandoned the city, fled south through the Iron Gate, and encamped on Great Snow Mountain. Baoyu pursued him to India.

sentences.zh: 帝駐大雪山前，時谷中雪深二丈，寶玉請封山川神。

translations.literal: The Emperor halted before Great Snow Mountain; at the time snow in the valley was twenty feet deep, and Baoyu requested enfeoffment of the mountain and river spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The Khan encamped before Great Snow Mountain, where snow lay twenty feet deep in the valleys. Baoyu requested that the mountain and river spirits be enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 壬午三月，封崑崙山為玄極王，大鹽池為惠濟王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the renwu year Kunlun Mountain was enfeoffed as King of the Mysterious Pole, and the Great Salt Lake as King of Beneficent Aid.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of renwu (1222), Kunlun Mountain was enfeoffed as King of the Mysterious Pole and the Great Salt Lake as King of Beneficent Aid.

sentences.zh: 從柘柏、速不台二先鋒收契丹、渤海等諸國，有功，累遷斷事官，卒于賀蘭山。

translations.literal: He followed the two vanguards Jebe and Subutai in reducing the Khitan, Bohai, and other states, performed merit, was repeatedly promoted to judicial officer, and died at Helan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the vanguards Jebe and Subutai in reducing the Khitan, Bohai, and other states, distinguished himself, rose to judicial officer, and died at Helan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 子德海，德山。

translations.literal: His sons were Dehai and Deshan.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Dehai and Deshan.

sentences.zh: 德山以萬戶破陝州，攻潼關，卒。

translations.literal: Deshan, as commander of ten thousand households, captured Shaanzhou and attacked Tong Pass, then died.
translations.idiomatic: Deshan, as commander of ten thousand households, captured Shaanzhou and attacked Tong Pass, then died.

sentences.zh: 子德海

translations.literal: His son Dehai
translations.idiomatic: His son Dehai

sentences.zh: 德海字大洋，資貌奇偉，亦通天文、兵法。

translations.literal: Dehai, courtesy name Dayang, was of extraordinary stature and appearance and likewise versed in astronomy and military science.
translations.idiomatic: Dehai, courtesy name Dayang, was of imposing stature and likewise versed in astronomy and military science.

sentences.zh: 金末，為謀克，擊宋將彭義斌於山東，敗之。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jin he was a mouke and attacked the Song general Peng Yibin in Shandong, defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jin he was a mouke and defeated the Song general Peng Yibin in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 知父寶玉北降，遁入太行山，大軍至，乃出降，為抄馬彈壓。

translations.literal: Learning that his father Baoyu had surrendered in the north, he fled into the Taihang Mountains; when the main army arrived he came out and surrendered and served as commander of mounted scouts for suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that his father had surrendered to the north, he fled into the Taihang Mountains. When the main army arrived he came out and surrendered, and served as commander of mounted scouts.

sentences.zh: 從先鋒柘柏西征，渡乞則里八海，攻鐵山，衣幟與敵軍不相辨，乃焚蒿為號，煙焰漫野，敵軍動，乘之，斬首三萬級。

translations.literal: He followed the vanguard Jebe on the western campaign, crossed Lake Qizili, attacked Tieshan, and when banners and dress could not be distinguished from the enemy's, burned artemisia as a signal; smoke and flame filled the fields, the enemy stirred, and seizing the moment they cut off thirty thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the vanguard Jebe on the western campaign, crossed Lake Qizili, and attacked Tieshan. When banners and dress could not be distinguished from the enemy's, he burned artemisia as a signal. Smoke filled the plain, the enemy stirred, and his troops cut down thirty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 踰雪嶺西北萬里，進軍次荅里國，悉平之。

translations.literal: Crossing Snow Ridge ten thousand li to the northwest, he advanced and halted at the kingdom of Daliguo, pacifying it entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing Snow Ridge ten thousand li to the northwest, he marched on and encamped at the kingdom of Daliguo, which he entirely subdued.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，還至崢山，吐蕃帥尼倫、回紇帥阿必丁反，復破斬之。

translations.literal: On the yiyou day he returned to Zhengshan. The Tibetan commander Nirun and the Uyghur commander Abiding rebelled; he again defeated and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day he returned to Zhengshan. The Tibetan commander Nirun and the Uyghur commander Abiding rose in revolt; he again routed them and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 戊子春，從元帥闊闊出游騎入關中，金人閉關拒守，德海引驍騎五百，斬關入，殺守者三百人，直擣風陵渡寨，後兵不至，引還。

translations.literal: In the spring of the wuzi year he followed Marshal Kuokuotai's raiding cavalry into Guanzhong. The Jin closed the passes and held them. Dehai led five hundred elite horsemen, forced a pass, killed three hundred defenders, and drove straight at the Fenglingdu fort. When the following troops failed to arrive, he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the wuzi year he followed Marshal Kuokuotai's raiding cavalry into Guanzhong. The Jin shut the passes and refused battle. Dehai led five hundred elite horsemen, broke through a pass, killed three hundred defenders, and struck straight at the Fenglingdu fort. When the rear columns failed to come up, he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 己丑秋，破南山八十三寨，陝西平。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the jichou year he stormed eighty-three fortified camps in the Southern Mountains, and Shaanxi was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the jichou year he captured eighty-three fortified camps in the Southern Mountains, and Shaanxi was brought under control.

sentences.zh: 德海導大將魁欲那拔都，假道漢中，歷荊、襄而東，與金將武僊軍十萬遇於白河，德海提孤軍轉戰，僊敗走，斬首二萬餘級，復破金移剌粘哥軍于鄧。

translations.literal: Dehai guided the great general Küyükbüke by a detour through Hanzhong, then east through Jing and Xiang. At the Bai River he met the Jin general Wuxian at the head of one hundred thousand men. Dehai fought on alone with a detached force; Wuxian was routed and fled, and more than twenty thousand heads were taken. He also defeated the Jin general Yelü Niange's army at Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Dehai guided the great general Küyükbüke by a detour through Hanzhong and then east through Jing and Xiang. At the Bai River he encountered the Jin general Wuxian with one hundred thousand men. Dehai fought on alone with a detached force, routed Wuxian, and took more than twenty thousand heads. He also defeated the Jin general Yelü Niange's army at Deng.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，至鈞州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter he reached Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter he arrived at Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛卯春正月，睿宗軍由洛陽來會于三峰山，金人溝地立軍圍之。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the xinmao year, Prince Ruizong's army came from Luoyang to rendezvous at Sanfeng Mountain. The Jin dug trenches and encamped to surround them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the xinmao year, Prince Ruizong's army marched from Luoyang to join forces at Sanfeng Mountain. The Jin dug trenches, established camps, and laid siege.

sentences.zh: 睿宗令軍中祈雪，又燒羊胛骨，卜得吉兆，夜大雪，深三尺，溝中軍僵立，刀槊凍不能舉。

translations.literal: Prince Ruizong ordered the army to pray for snow and burned sheep shoulder blades for divination, obtaining an auspicious sign. That night snow fell heavily to a depth of three chi. The Jin troops in the trenches stood frozen stiff, their blades and spears too ice-bound to lift.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ruizong ordered the army to pray for snow and burned sheep shoulder blades for divination until an auspicious omen appeared. That night snow fell heavily to a depth of three chi. The Jin troops in the trenches stood frozen stiff, unable to raise their blades and spears.

sentences.zh: 我軍衝圍而出，金人死者三十餘萬，其帥完顏哈達、移剌蒲兀走匿浮圖上，德海命掘浮圖基，出其柱而焚之，完顏斜烈單騎遁還洛陽。

translations.literal: Our army broke through the encirclement. More than three hundred thousand Jin soldiers were killed. Their commanders Wanyan Hada and Yelü Puwu fled and hid atop a pagoda. Dehai ordered the pagoda foundation dug up, its pillars removed, and the structure burned. Wanyan Xielie escaped alone on horseback back to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Our army broke through the siege. More than three hundred thousand Jin soldiers were killed. Their commanders Wanyan Hada and Yelü Puwu fled and hid atop a pagoda. Dehai ordered the pagoda undermined, its pillars pulled out, and the structure burned down. Wanyan Xielie escaped alone on horseback to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 又破金將合喜兵於中牟，完顏斜烈復帥軍十萬來拒，戰于鄭，先登破之，殺其都尉左崇。

translations.literal: He again defeated the Jin general Hexi's army at Zhongmou. Wanyan Xielie again led one hundred thousand men to resist. At Zheng, Dehai was first over the walls and broke the enemy force, killing their commandant Zuo Chong.
translations.idiomatic: He again defeated the Jin general Hexi's army at Zhongmou. Wanyan Xielie once more led one hundred thousand men to resist. At Zheng, Dehai was first over the walls, broke the enemy, and killed their commandant Zuo Chong.

sentences.zh: 以功遷右監軍。

translations.literal: For these achievements he was promoted to Right Army Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was promoted to Right Army Supervisor.

sentences.zh: 壬辰正月，破金師於黃龍岡。

translations.literal: In the first month of the renchen year he defeated the Jin army at Huanglong Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the renchen year he routed the Jin army at Huanglong Ridge.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，取申、唐二州。

translations.literal: On the guisi day he captured the two prefectures of Shen and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: On the guisi day he took the two prefectures of Shen and Tang.

sentences.zh: 甲午，河南復叛，德海往討之，砲傷其足，以疾歸，卒。

translations.literal: On the jiawu day Henan rebelled again. Dehai went to suppress the revolt but was wounded in the foot by cannon fire. He returned home ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day Henan rebelled again. Dehai marched to suppress the revolt but was wounded in the foot by cannon fire. He returned home on account of illness and died.

sentences.zh: 先是，太宗詔大臣忽都虎等試天下僧尼道士，選精通經文者千人，有能工藝者，則命小通事合住等領之，餘皆為民。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Taizong had decreed that the minister Huduhu and others examine Buddhist monks, nuns, and Daoist priests throughout the realm. One thousand who were proficient in scripture were selected; those skilled in crafts were placed under the junior interpreter Hezhu and others, and the remainder were returned to common life.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Taizong had decreed that the minister Huduhu and others examine Buddhist monks, nuns, and Daoist priests throughout the realm. One thousand who were proficient in scripture were retained; those skilled in crafts were assigned to the junior interpreter Hezhu and others, and the rest were returned to lay life.

sentences.zh: 又詔天下置學廩，育人材，立科目，選之入仕，皆從德海之請也。

translations.literal: The emperor also decreed that academies be established throughout the realm to nurture talent, that examination categories be instituted, and that successful candidates be selected for office—all at Dehai's request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also decreed that academies be established throughout the realm to nurture talent, that civil service categories be created, and that successful candidates be selected for office—all at Dehai's request.

sentences.zh: 子侃。

translations.literal: His son was Kan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Kan.

sentences.zh: 德海子侃

translations.literal: Dehai's Son Kan
translations.idiomatic: Dehai's Son Kan

sentences.zh: 侃字仲和，幼為丞相史天澤所器重，留于家而教養之。

translations.literal: Kan, courtesy name Zhonghe, was greatly valued in his youth by the chancellor Shi Tianze, who kept him in his household to raise and educate him.
translations.idiomatic: Kan, courtesy name Zhonghe, was greatly valued in his youth by Chancellor Shi Tianze, who kept him in his home to raise and educate him.

sentences.zh: 弱冠為百戶，鷙勇有謀略。

translations.literal: At twenty he became a centurion—fierce, courageous, and skilled in strategy.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he became a centurion—fierce, courageous, and possessed of strategic talent.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，金將伯撒復取衛州，侃拒之，破其兵四萬於新衛州。

translations.literal: In the renchen year the Jin general Bosa recaptured Weizhou. Kan met him in resistance and destroyed his force of forty thousand at New Weizhou.
