translations.idiomatic: In the renchen year the Jin general Bosa recaptured Weizhou. Kan resisted him and destroyed his army of forty thousand at New Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 遂渡河，襲金主，至歸德，敗其兵於閼伯臺，即從速不台攻汴西門，金元帥崔立降。

translations.literal: He then crossed the river to strike at the Jin emperor, reached Guide, and defeated the Jin army at Yuebota. He then followed Subutai in the assault on the west gate of Bianjing, where the Jin marshal Cui Li surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He then crossed the river to strike at the Jin emperor, reached Guide, and defeated the Jin army at Yuebota. He then followed Subutai in the assault on the west gate of Bianjing, where the Jin marshal Cui Li surrendered.

sentences.zh: 以功授緫把。

translations.literal: For his achievements he was appointed chief commander (zongba).
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was appointed chief commander.

sentences.zh: 從天澤屯太康，復以下德安功為千戶。

translations.literal: He followed Tianze in garrison at Taikang and was again made commander of a thousand households for his merit in capturing De'an.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Tianze in garrison at Taikang and was again made commander of a thousand households for his merit in taking De'an.

sentences.zh: 壬子，送兵仗至和林，改抄馬那顏。

translations.literal: In the renzi year he delivered arms to Karakorum and was reassigned as chaoma nayin, commander of mounted scouts.
translations.idiomatic: In the renzi year he delivered arms to Karakorum and was reassigned as chaoma nayin, commander of mounted scouts.

sentences.zh: 從宗王旭烈兀西征。

translations.literal: He followed Prince Hulagu on the western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince Hulagu on the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，至木乃兮。

translations.literal: On the guichou day he reached Munakke.
translations.idiomatic: On the guichou day he reached Munakke.

sentences.zh: 其國塹道，置毒水中，侃破其兵五萬，下一百二十八城，斬其將忽都荅而兀朱筭灘。

translations.literal: That kingdom had ditches filled with poisoned water. Kan destroyed their army of fifty thousand, captured one hundred twenty-eight cities, and beheaded their general Qutay and Prince Wuzhu.
translations.idiomatic: That kingdom had ditches filled with poisoned water. Kan destroyed their army of fifty thousand, captured one hundred twenty-eight cities, and beheaded their general Qutay and Prince Wuzhu.

sentences.zh: 筭灘，華言王也。

translations.literal: Suanban means "king" in Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Suanban means "king" in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，至乞都卜。

translations.literal: On the bingchen day he reached Kitab.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen day he reached Kitab.

sentences.zh: 其城在擔寒山上，懸梯上下，守以精兵悍卒，乃築夾城圍之，莫能克。

translations.literal: The city stood on Dahan Mountain, reached only by ropes and ladders. Elite troops and fierce soldiers held it. They built a double wall of siege works around it but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The city stood on Dahan Mountain and could be reached only by ropes and ladders. Elite troops and fierce soldiers defended it. The besiegers built a double ring of siege works around it but could not capture it.

sentences.zh: 侃架砲攻之，守將火者納失兒開門降。

translations.literal: Kan set up siege cannon to attack. The defending general Khaja Nasir opened the gates and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Kan set up siege cannon to attack. The defending general Khaja Nasir opened the gates and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 旭烈兀遣侃往說兀魯兀乃筭灘來降。

translations.literal: Hulagu sent Kan to persuade Prince Ulugunan to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Hulagu sent Kan to persuade Prince Ulugunan to surrender.

sentences.zh: 其父阿力據西城，侃攻破之，走據東城，復攻破殺之。

translations.literal: His father Ali held the west city. Kan stormed it. Ali fled to the east city, which Kan also stormed and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ali held the west city. Kan stormed it. Ali fled to the east city, which Kan stormed as well and killed him.

sentences.zh: 丁巳正月，至兀里兒城，伏兵，下令聞鉦聲則起。

translations.literal: In the first month of the dingsi year he reached the city of Wulier, set an ambush, and ordered his men to rise at the sound of the gong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the dingsi year he reached the city of Wulier, laid an ambush, and ordered his men to rise at the sound of the gong.

sentences.zh: 敵兵果來，伏發，盡殺之，海牙筭灘降。

translations.literal: When the enemy came as expected, the ambush sprang and wiped them out. Prince Hayya submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy came as expected, the ambush sprang and wiped them out. Prince Hayya surrendered.

sentences.zh: 又西至阿剌汀，破其游兵三萬，禡拶荅而筭攤降。

translations.literal: Advancing west to Alatin, he routed their roaming force of thirty thousand. Prince Mazasadai submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing west to Alatin, he routed their roaming force of thirty thousand. Prince Mazasadai surrendered.

sentences.zh: 至乞石迷部，忽里筭灘降。

translations.literal: When he reached the Qishimi region, Prince Huli submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the Qishimi region, Prince Huli surrendered.

sentences.zh: 西戎大國也，地方八千里，父子相傳四十二世，勝兵數十萬。

translations.literal: It was a great state of the Western Regions, eight thousand li in extent, with forty-two generations of father-to-son succession and several hundred thousand men under arms.
translations.idiomatic: It was a great state of the Western Regions, eight thousand li in extent, with forty-two generations of father-to-son rule and several hundred thousand men under arms.

sentences.zh: 侃兵至，破其兵七萬，屠西城。

translations.literal: When Kan's army arrived, it destroyed their force of seventy thousand and sacked the west city.
translations.idiomatic: When Kan's army arrived, it destroyed their force of seventy thousand and sacked the west city.

sentences.zh: 又破其東城，東城殿宇，皆搆以沉檀木，舉火焚之，香聞百里，得七十二弦琵琶、五尺珊瑚燈檠。

translations.literal: He then stormed the east city. Its halls were built entirely of agarwood; he set them alight, and the fragrance was smelled for a hundred li. Among the spoils were a seventy-two-string pipa and a five-chi coral lamp stand.
translations.idiomatic: He then stormed the east city. Its halls were built entirely of agarwood; he set them ablaze, and the fragrance carried for a hundred li. Among the spoils were a seventy-two-string pipa and a five-chi coral lamp stand.

sentences.zh: 兩城間有大河，侃預造浮梁以防其遁。

translations.literal: A great river lay between the two cities. Kan had a pontoon bridge built in advance to block their escape.
translations.idiomatic: A great river lay between the two cities. Kan had a pontoon bridge built in advance to prevent their escape.

sentences.zh: 城破，合里法筭灘登舟，睹河有浮梁扼之，乃自縛詣軍門降。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Prince Helifa boarded a boat but saw the pontoon bridge blocking the river. He bound himself and came to the camp gate to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Prince Helifa boarded a boat but saw the pontoon bridge blocking the river. He bound himself and came to the camp gate to surrender.

sentences.zh: 其將紂荅兒遁去，侃追之，至暮，諸軍欲頓舍，侃不聽，又行十餘里，乃止。

translations.literal: Their general Zhoudaer fled. Kan pursued him. At dusk the troops wished to make camp, but Kan refused and marched another ten-odd li before halting.
translations.idiomatic: Their general Zhoudaer fled. Kan pursued him. At dusk the troops wished to make camp, but Kan refused and marched another ten-odd li before stopping.

sentences.zh: 夜暴雨，先所欲舍處水深數尺。

translations.literal: That night a violent storm broke. Where they had meant to camp, the water stood several chi deep.
translations.idiomatic: That night a violent storm broke. Where they had meant to camp, the water stood several chi deep.

sentences.zh: 明日，獲紂荅兒，斬之，拔三百餘城。

translations.literal: The next day they captured Zhoudaer and beheaded him, and took more than three hundred cities.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they captured Zhoudaer and beheaded him, and took more than three hundred cities.

sentences.zh: 又西行三千里，至天房，其將住石致書請降，左右以住石之請為信然，易之不為備，侃曰：「欺敵者亡，軍機多詐，若中彼計，恥莫大焉。」

translations.literal: Advancing another three thousand li west, he reached Tianfang. Its general Zhushi sent a letter requesting surrender. The attendants thought Zhushi's request genuine and treated it lightly, making no preparations. Kan said, "He who underestimates the enemy is doomed. Military affairs are full of deception. If we fall into their trap, there is no greater shame."
translations.idiomatic: Advancing another three thousand li west, he reached Tianfang. Its general Zhushi sent a letter requesting surrender. The attendants took the offer at face value and made no preparations. Kan said, "He who underestimates the enemy is doomed. War is full of deception. If we fall into their trap, there is no greater disgrace."

sentences.zh: 乃嚴備以待。

translations.literal: He then made strict preparations and waited.
translations.idiomatic: He then made strict preparations and waited.

sentences.zh: 住石果來邀我師，侃與戰，大敗之，巴兒筭灘降，下其城一百八十五。

translations.literal: Zhushi indeed came to ambush our army. Kan gave battle and routed him utterly. Prince Ba'er submitted, and one hundred eighty-five cities were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Zhushi indeed came to ambush our army. Kan gave battle and routed him completely. Prince Ba'er surrendered, and one hundred eighty-five cities were taken.

sentences.zh: 又西行四十里，至密昔兒。

translations.literal: Advancing another forty li west, he reached Misr.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing another forty li west, he reached Misr.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，已休，復驅兵起，留數病卒，西行十餘里頓軍，下令軍中，銜枚轉箭。

translations.literal: At dusk, after the men had already settled to rest, he roused the army again. He left a few sick soldiers behind, marched west for ten-odd li and encamped, ordering the men to hold arrows in their mouths and maintain silence.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk, after the men had already settled to rest, he roused the army again. He left a few sick soldiers behind, marched west for ten-odd li and encamped, ordering the men to hold arrows in their mouths and keep silent.

sentences.zh: 敵不知也，潛兵夜來襲，殺病卒，可乃筭灘大驚曰：「東天將軍，神人也。」

translations.literal: The enemy did not know. Hidden troops came by night to attack and killed the sick soldiers. Prince Kena was greatly alarmed and said, "The Eastern Heaven General is a divine man."
translations.idiomatic: The enemy knew nothing of this. Hidden troops came by night to attack and killed the sick soldiers. Prince Kena was greatly alarmed and said, "The Eastern Heaven General is a divine man."

sentences.zh: 遂降。

translations.literal: He then submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 戊午，旭烈兀命侃西渡海，收富浪。

translations.literal: On the wuwu day Hulagu ordered Kan to cross the sea westward and subdue Folang.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day Hulagu ordered Kan to cross the sea westward and subdue Folang.

sentences.zh: 侃喻以禍福，兀都筭灘曰：「吾昨所夢神人，乃將軍也。」

translations.literal: Kan admonished him with talk of fortune and calamity. Prince Wudu said, "The divine man I dreamed of yesterday is precisely the general."
translations.idiomatic: Kan admonished him with talk of fortune and calamity. Prince Wudu said, "The divine man I dreamed of yesterday is none other than the general."

sentences.zh: 即來降。

translations.literal: He immediately came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately came to surrender.

sentences.zh: 師還，西南至石羅子，敵人來拒，侃直出掠陣，一鼓敗之，換斯干阿荅畢筭灘降。

translations.literal: The army returned and marched southwest to Shiluozi. The enemy came to resist. Kan charged straight out and raided their formation; at the first drumbeat he defeated them. Prince Huansigan A'dabi submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The army returned and marched southwest to Shiluozi. The enemy came to resist. Kan charged straight out and broke their formation; at the first drumbeat he defeated them. Prince Huansigan A'dabi surrendered.

sentences.zh: 至賓鐵，侃以奇兵奄擊，大敗之，加葉筭灘降。

translations.literal: At Bintie, Kan struck suddenly with a surprise force and routed the enemy. Prince Jiaye submitted.
translations.idiomatic: At Bintie, Kan struck suddenly with a surprise force and routed the enemy. Prince Jiaye surrendered.

sentences.zh: 己未，破兀林游兵四萬，阿必丁筭灘大懼，來降，得城一百二十。

translations.literal: On the jiwei day he routed Wulin's roaming army of forty thousand. Prince Abiding was greatly afraid and came to submit, yielding one hundred twenty cities.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei day he routed Wulin's roaming army of forty thousand. Prince Abiding was greatly afraid and surrendered, yielding one hundred twenty cities.

sentences.zh: 西南至乞里彎，忽都馬丁筭灘來降。

translations.literal: Marching southwest to Qiliwan, Prince Hudu Mading came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Marching southwest to Qiliwan, Prince Hudu Mading came to surrender.

sentences.zh: 西域平。

translations.literal: The Western Regions were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Regions were pacified.

sentences.zh: 侃以捷告至釣魚山，會憲宗崩，乃還鄧，開屯田，立保障。

translations.literal: Kan sent word of victory as far as Diaoyu Mountain. Learning of Emperor Xianzong's death, he returned to Deng, opened military colonies, and established defensive posts.
translations.idiomatic: Kan sent word of victory as far as Diaoyu Mountain. Learning of Emperor Xianzong's death, he returned to Deng, opened military colonies, and established defensive posts.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，擢江漢大都督府理問官。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Zhongtong era he was promoted to judicial inquirer of the Jianghan Grand Military Governor's office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhongtong era he was promoted to judicial inquirer of the Jianghan Grand Military Governor's office.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，益都李璮及徐州緫管李杲哥俱反，宋夏貴復來犯邊。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year, Li Tan of Yidu and Li Gaoge, commander of Xuzhou, both rebelled, and the Song general Xia Gui again invaded the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year, Li Tan of Yidu and Li Gaoge, commander of Xuzhou, both rebelled, and the Song general Xia Gui again invaded the frontier.

sentences.zh: 史天澤薦侃，召入見，世祖問計所出，曰：「群盜竊發，猶柙中虎。

translations.literal: Shi Tianze recommended Kan, who was summoned to audience. Emperor Shizu asked what plan he proposed. He said, "When bandits rise in rebellion, they are like tigers in a cage.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tianze recommended Kan, who was summoned to audience. Emperor Shizu asked what plan he proposed. He said, "When bandits rise in rebellion, they are like tigers in a cage.

sentences.zh: 內無資糧，外無救援，築城環之，坐待其困，計日可擒也。」

translations.literal: With no supplies within and no relief from without, encircle them with fortifications and wait for them to wear themselves out—they can be captured within days."
translations.idiomatic: With no supplies within and no relief from without, encircle them with fortifications and wait for them to exhaust themselves—they can be captured within days."

sentences.zh: 帝然之，賜尚衣弓矢。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and granted him imperial robes, a bow, and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and granted him imperial robes, a bow, and arrows.

sentences.zh: 馳至徐，斬杲哥。

translations.literal: He galloped to Xuzhou and beheaded Gaoge.
translations.idiomatic: He galloped to Xuzhou and beheaded Gaoge.

sentences.zh: 夏貴焚廬舍，徙軍民南去，侃追貴，過宿遷縣，奪軍民萬餘人而還。

translations.literal: Xia Gui burned dwellings and withdrew troops and civilians southward. Kan pursued Xia Gui, passed through Suqian County, and brought back more than ten thousand troops and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Gui burned dwellings and withdrew troops and civilians southward. Kan pursued Xia Gui, passed through Suqian County, and brought back more than ten thousand troops and civilians.

sentences.zh: 賜金符，為徐、邳二州緫管。

translations.literal: He was granted a gold tally and made commander of the two prefectures of Xu and Pi.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a gold tally and made commander of the two prefectures of Xu and Pi.

sentences.zh: 杲哥之弟驢馬，復與夏貴以兵三萬來擾邊境，侃出戰，斬首千餘級，奪戰艦二百。

translations.literal: Gaoge's younger brother Lüma again joined Xia Gui with thirty thousand men to raid the border. Kan gave battle, took more than a thousand heads, and captured two hundred warships.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoge's younger brother Lüma again joined Xia Gui with thirty thousand men to raid the border. Kan gave battle, took more than a thousand heads, and captured two hundred warships.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，有言當解史天澤兵權者，天澤遂遷他官，侃亦調同知滕州。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Zhiyuan era, amid talk that Shi Tianze's military authority should be removed, Tianze was transferred to another post and Kan was reassigned as deputy prefect of Tengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhiyuan era, amid talk that Shi Tianze's military authority should be removed, Tianze was transferred to another post and Kan was reassigned as deputy prefect of Tengzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，侃上言：「宋人羈留我使，宜興師問罪。

translations.literal: In the third year Kan memorialized: "The Song have detained our envoys. We ought to raise an army and demand redress.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Kan memorialized: "The Song have detained our envoys. We ought to raise an army and demand redress.

sentences.zh: 淮北可立屯田三百六十所，每屯置牛三百六十具，計一屯所出，足供軍旅一日之需。」

translations.literal: North of the Huai, three hundred sixty military colonies could be established. Each colony would be furnished with three hundred sixty teams of oxen, and the output of one colony would suffice to supply an army for one day."
translations.idiomatic: North of the Huai, three hundred sixty military colonies could be established. Each colony would be furnished with three hundred sixty teams of oxen, and the output of one colony would suffice to supply an army for one day."

sentences.zh: 四年，徙高唐令，兼治夏津、武城等五縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred as magistrate of Gaotang and concurrently administered Xiajin, Wucheng, and four other counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred as magistrate of Gaotang and concurrently administered Xiajin, Wucheng, and four other counties.

sentences.zh: 五年，邑人吳乞兒、濟南道士胡王反，討平之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the local man Wu Qi'er and the Jinan Daoist Hu Wang rebelled; he suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the local man Wu Qi'er and the Jinan Daoist Hu Wang rebelled; he suppressed and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 七年，改白馬令，僧臧羅漢與彰德趙當驢反，又平之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was reassigned as magistrate of Baima. The monk Zang Luohan and Zhao Danglü of Zhangde rebelled, and he pacified them as well.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was reassigned as magistrate of Baima. The monk Zang Luohan and Zhao Danglü of Zhangde rebelled, and he pacified them as well.

sentences.zh: 帝以侃習於軍務，擢為萬戶，從軍下襄陽，由陽羅上流渡江。

translations.literal: Because Kan was versed in military affairs, the emperor promoted him to commander of ten thousand households. He followed the army in the capture of Xiangyang and crossed the Yangzi at the upper reaches of Yangluo.
translations.idiomatic: Because Kan was versed in military affairs, the emperor promoted him to commander of ten thousand households. He followed the army in the capture of Xiangyang and crossed the Yangzi at the upper reaches of Yangluo.

sentences.zh: 江南平，遷知寧海州，居一年，卒。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified, he was transferred as prefect of Ninghaizhou. After one year in office he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangnan was pacified, he was transferred as prefect of Ninghaizhou. After one year in office he died.

sentences.zh: 侃行軍有紀律，野爨露宿，雖風雨不入民舍，所至興學課農，吏民畏服。

translations.literal: Kan maintained strict discipline on campaign, cooking in the open and sleeping under the sky; even in wind and rain his men did not enter civilian houses. Wherever he went he established schools and urged agriculture, and officials and common people alike feared and respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Kan maintained strict discipline on campaign, cooking in the open and sleeping under the sky; even in wind and rain his men did not enter civilian houses. Wherever he went he established schools and urged agriculture, and officials and common people alike feared and respected him.

sentences.zh: 子秉仁、秉義。

translations.literal: His sons were Bingren and Bingyi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Bingren and Bingyi.

sentences.zh: 石天應

translations.literal: Shi Tianying
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tianying

sentences.zh: 石天應字瑞之，興中永德人。

translations.literal: Shi Tianying, courtesy name Ruizhi, was a native of Yongde in Xingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tianying, courtesy name Ruizhi, was a native of Yongde in Xingzhong.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，豪爽不羈，頗知讀書，鄉里人多歸之。

translations.literal: He was skilled in riding and archery, bold and generous and unrestrained by convention, and well versed in books; many in his village followed him.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in riding and archery, bold and generous and unrestrained by convention, and well versed in books; many in his village followed him.

sentences.zh: 太祖時，太師、國王木華黎南下，天應率衆迎謁軍門。

translations.literal: In the time of Taizu, the Grand Preceptor and Prince Muqali marched south. Tianying led his followers to welcome him at the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the time of Taizu, the Grand Preceptor and Prince Muqali marched south. Tianying led his followers to welcome him at the army gate.

sentences.zh: 木華黎即承制授興中府尹、兵馬都提控，俾從南征。

translations.literal: Muqali immediately by imperial commission appointed him prefect of Xingzhong and commander of all troops and horses, and ordered him to follow the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali immediately by imperial commission appointed him prefect of Xingzhong and commander of all troops and horses, and ordered him to follow the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 天應造戰攻之具，臨機應變，捷出如神，以功拜龍虎衛上將軍、元帥右監軍，戍燕。

translations.literal: Tianying made siege and assault equipment, adapted to circumstances with swift responses like those of a divine hand, and for his achievements was appointed senior general of the Longhu Guard and Right Army Supervisor of the marshal, garrisoning Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Tianying made siege and assault equipment, adapted to circumstances with swift responses like those of a divine hand, and for his achievements was appointed senior general of the Longhu Guard and Right Army Supervisor of the marshal, garrisoning Yan.

sentences.zh: 天應旌旗色用黑，人目之曰黑軍。

translations.literal: Tianying's banners and flags were black, and people called them the Black Army.
translations.idiomatic: Tianying's banners and flags were black, and people called them the Black Army.

sentences.zh: 屢從木華黎，大小二百餘戰，常以身先士卒，累功遷右副元帥。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed Muqali through more than two hundred battles large and small, often leading the troops in person ahead of the ranks, and through accumulated merit was promoted to Right Vice Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly followed Muqali through more than two hundred battles large and small, often leading the troops in person ahead of the ranks, and through accumulated merit was promoted to Right Vice Marshal.

sentences.zh: 辛巳秋八月，從木華黎征陝右，假道西夏，自東勝濟河，南攻葭州拔之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn in the xinsi year he followed Muqali in campaigning in western Shaanxi. By a detour through Western Xia, from Dongsheng he crossed the river and attacked Jiazhou to the south, capturing it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn in the xinsi year he followed Muqali in campaigning in western Shaanxi. By a detour through Western Xia, from Dongsheng he crossed the river and attacked Jiazhou to the south, capturing it.

sentences.zh: 天應因說太師曰：「西戎雖降，實未可信。

translations.literal: Tianying thereupon advised the Grand Preceptor: "Although the Western Rong have submitted, in truth they cannot yet be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Tianying thereupon advised the Grand Preceptor: "Although the Western Rong have submitted, in truth they cannot yet be trusted.

sentences.zh: 此州當金、夏之衝，居人健勇，倉庫豐實，加以長河為限，脫為敵軍所梗，緩急非便，宜命將守之，多造舟楫，以備不虞，此萬世計也。」

translations.literal: This prefecture stands at the crossroads of Jin and Xia. Its inhabitants are hardy and brave, its storehouses abundant. With the long river as a barrier, if enemy forces should block it, neither advance nor retreat would be convenient. A general ought to be appointed to garrison it and many boats built to guard against the unexpected. This is a plan for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: This prefecture stands at the crossroads of Jin and Xia. Its inhabitants are hardy and brave, its storehouses abundant. With the long river as a barrier, if enemy forces should block it, neither advance nor retreat would be convenient. A general ought to be appointed to garrison it and many boats built to guard against the unexpected. This is a plan for ten thousand generations."

sentences.zh: 木華黎然之，表授金紫光祿大夫、陝西河東路行臺兵馬都元帥，以勁兵五千，留守葭蘆。

translations.literal: Muqali approved. By memorial he was appointed Golden Purple Light Grandee and marshal of all troops of the Shaanxi Hedong Circuit Mobile Bureau, and with five thousand elite troops he remained to garrison Jialu.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali approved. By memorial he was appointed Golden Purple Light Grandee and marshal of all troops of the Shaanxi Hedong Circuit Mobile Bureau, and with five thousand elite troops he remained to garrison Jialu.

sentences.zh: 遂造舟楫，建浮橋，諸將多言水漲波惡，恐勞費無功，天應下令曰：「有沮吾事者，斷其舌！」

translations.literal: He then built boats and constructed a floating bridge. Many generals said the water was swollen and the waves fierce, fearing labor and expense without result. Tianying issued an order: "Whoever obstructs my work, I shall cut off his tongue!"
translations.idiomatic: He then built boats and constructed a floating bridge. Many generals said the water was swollen and the waves fierce, fearing labor and expense without result. Tianying issued an order: "Whoever obstructs my work, I shall cut off his tongue!"

sentences.zh: 橋成，諸將悅服。

translations.literal: When the bridge was completed, the generals were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the bridge was completed, the generals were pleased and submitted.

sentences.zh: 先時，葭守王公佐收合餘燼，攻函谷關，將圖復故地，及見橋成，遂潰去。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jia's defender Wang Gongzuo had gathered the remaining embers of resistance, attacked Hangu Pass, and was about to plan the recovery of the old territory. When he saw the bridge completed, he routed and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jia's defender Wang Gongzuo had gathered the remaining embers of resistance, attacked Hangu Pass, and was about to plan the recovery of the old territory. When he saw the bridge completed, he routed and fled.

sentences.zh: 於是分兵四出，悉定葭、綏之地。

translations.literal: Thereupon he divided his troops in four directions and entirely pacified the territories of Jia and Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he divided his troops in four directions and entirely pacified the territories of Jia and Sui.

sentences.zh: 一日，謁木華黎於汾水東，木華黎諭以進取之策。

translations.literal: One day he visited Muqali east of the Fen River, and Muqali instructed him in a strategy of advance and capture.
translations.idiomatic: One day he visited Muqali east of the Fen River, and Muqali instructed him in a strategy of advance and capture.

sentences.zh: 天應還鎮，召將佐謂曰：「吾累卿等留屯於此，今聞河中東西皆平川廣野，可以駐軍，規取關陝，諸君以為如何？」

translations.literal: Tianying returned to his garrison and summoned his generals and staff, saying, "I have burdened you all with remaining garrisoned here. Now I hear that east and west of Hezhong are all flat plains and broad fields where troops can be stationed, and that we may plan to take Guan and Shaan. What do you gentlemen think?"
translations.idiomatic: Tianying returned to his garrison and summoned his generals and staff, saying, "I have burdened you all with remaining garrisoned here. Now I hear that east and west of Hezhong are all flat plains and broad fields where troops can be stationed, and that we may plan to take Guan and Shaan. What do you gentlemen think?"

sentences.zh: 或諫曰：「河中雖用武之地，南有潼關，西有京兆，皆金軍所屯；

translations.literal: Someone remonstrated: "Although Hezhong is ground fit for war, to the south is Tong Pass and to the west is Jingzhao, both garrisoned by Jin troops;
translations.idiomatic: Someone remonstrated: "Although Hezhong is ground fit for war, to the south is Tong Pass and to the west is Jingzhao, both garrisoned by Jin troops;

sentences.zh: 且民新附，其心未一，守之恐貽噬臍之悔。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the people have newly submitted and their hearts are not yet one; to hold it may bring the regret of biting one's own navel."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, these people have only just submitted and their loyalties remain divided. To garrison the place would risk remorse we could never undo."

sentences.zh: 天應曰：「葭州正通鄜、延，今鄜已平，延不孤立，若發國書，令夏人取之，猶掌中物耳。

translations.literal: Tianying replied: "Jiazhou lies directly on the route to Fu and Yan. Now Fu is pacified and Yan will not stand alone. If we send a state letter ordering the Xia people to take it, it will be like something in the palm of the hand.
translations.idiomatic: Tianying replied: "Jiazhou sits on the road to Fu and Yan. Fu is already pacified, so Yan cannot hold out alone. Send a letter under the imperial seal and let the Xia take it—it will be as easy as closing one's fist around it.

sentences.zh: 且國家之急，本在河南，此州路險地僻，轉餉甚難，河中雖迫於二鎮，實用武立功之地，北接汾、晉，西連同、華，地五千餘里，戶數十萬，若起漕運以通餽餉，則關內可剋期而定，關內既定，長河以南，在吾目中矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, the state's urgent need lies fundamentally south of the Yellow River. This prefecture has perilous roads and remote lands; transporting provisions is very difficult. Although Hezhong is pressed by two garrison commands, it is in truth ground where martial merit may be won. North it connects to Fen and Jin; west it links with Tong and Hua. Its territory extends more than five thousand li, with households numbering in the tens of thousands. If we establish canal transport to open supply lines, then the land within the passes can be settled within a set term. Once the interior is settled, everything south of the long river will be within our sight.
translations.idiomatic: The empire's true urgency lies south of the Yellow River. This region's roads are treacherous and its land remote, making supply a constant struggle. Hezhong may be squeezed between two enemy garrisons, yet it is ground where a warrior can win lasting fame. It borders Fen and Jin to the north and Tong and Hua to the west—more than five thousand li of territory and tens of thousands of households. Open the grain routes by canal, and the interior can be secured on schedule. Once the passes are ours, everything south of the long river will lie open before us.

sentences.zh: 吾年垂六十，老耄將至，一旦卧病床第，聞後生輩立功名，死不瞑目矣。

translations.literal: I am nearing sixty; old age and senility are close at hand. If I should one day lie sick upon my bed and hear the younger generation winning fame, I could not close my eyes in death.
translations.idiomatic: I am nearly sixty, and feebleness is not far off. If I should fall ill and hear the young winning glory while I lie helpless, I would die with my eyes open.

sentences.zh: 男兒要當死戰陣以報國，是吾志也！」

translations.literal: A man ought to die on the battlefield in service of the state — that is my resolve!"
translations.idiomatic: A man should die fighting for his country—that is my purpose!"

sentences.zh: 秋九月，遂移軍河中。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn, he then moved his army to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn, he moved his army to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 既而金軍果潛入中條，襲河中。

translations.literal: Before long, Jin troops did steal through the Zhongtiao Mountains and assault Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Jin forces slipped through the Zhongtiao range and struck at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 天應知之，先遣驍將吳澤伏兵要路。

translations.literal: Tianying learned of it and first dispatched the fierce general Wu Ze to lay ambush on the critical road.
translations.idiomatic: Tianying learned of the threat and sent the fierce general Wu Ze ahead to ambush the vital road.

sentences.zh: 澤勇而嗜酒，是夕，方醉卧林中，金兵由間道已直抵城下。

translations.literal: Ze was brave but fond of wine. That evening, while he lay drunk asleep in the forest, Jin soldiers by a hidden path had already reached straight beneath the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Ze was brave but loved his wine. That night he lay drunk in the woods while Jin troops, taking a hidden path, marched straight to the foot of the walls.

sentences.zh: 時兵燼後，守具未完，新附者爭縋而去，敵乘隙入。

translations.literal: At the time, after the embers of war, the defensive equipment was not yet complete. Those newly submitted scrambled to descend by rope and flee. The enemy seized the opening and entered.
translations.idiomatic: The city was still rebuilding from the fires of war; its defenses were unfinished. Newly submitted troops scrambled down ropes to escape, and the enemy poured through the breach.

sentences.zh: 天應見火舉，知敵已入，奮身角戰，左右從者四十餘騎，皆曰：「吳澤誤我。」

translations.literal: Tianying saw signal fires raised and knew the enemy had entered. He threw himself into hand-to-hand combat. The forty-odd horsemen who followed him on either side all said, "Wu Ze has ruined us."
translations.idiomatic: Tianying saw the signal fires and knew the enemy was inside the walls. He threw himself into the melee. The forty-odd horsemen at his side cried out, "Wu Ze has betrayed us!"

sentences.zh: 或勸西渡河，天應曰：「先時人諫我南遷，吾違衆而來此，事急棄去，是不武也。

translations.literal: Some urged him to cross the river westward. Tianying said, "Earlier men remonstrated with me against moving south. I defied the multitude and came here. To abandon the place in crisis would be unworthy of a warrior.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to flee west across the river. Tianying said, "Men warned me against coming south. I defied them and came here. To abandon the city now would be cowardice unworthy of a soldier.

sentences.zh: 縱太師不罪我，何面目以見同列乎！

translations.literal: Even if the Grand Preceptor does not punish me, with what face could I meet my peers!
translations.idiomatic: Even if the Grand Preceptor spared me, how could I face my comrades again!

sentences.zh: 今日惟死而已，汝等勉之。」

translations.literal: Today there is nothing but death. Do your utmost."
translations.idiomatic: Today we die—that is all. Do your best."

sentences.zh: 少頃，敵兵四合，天應飲血力戰，至日午，死之。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, enemy troops closed in from all four sides. Tianying drank blood and fought with all his strength until midday, when he died.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later the enemy closed in from every side. Tianying fought on, blood in his mouth, until noon, when he fell.

sentences.zh: 木華黎聞而痛惜焉。

translations.literal: Muqali heard and grieved deeply.
translations.idiomatic: When Muqali heard, he mourned the loss bitterly.

sentences.zh: 子煥中，知興中府事；

translations.literal: His son Huanzhong served as administrator of Xingzhong Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: His son Huanzhong served as administrator of Xingzhong Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 執中，行軍千戶；

translations.literal: Zhizhong was a mobile chiliarch;
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong was a mobile chiliarch;

sentences.zh: 受中，興中府相副官。

translations.literal: Shouzhong was deputy officer of Xingzhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhong was deputy officer of Xingzhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，天應死事時，弟天禹子佐中在軍中。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Tianying died in battle, his younger brother Tianyu's son Zuozhong was in the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianying fell in battle, his younger brother Tianyu's son Zuozhong was serving in the army.

sentences.zh: 伺敵少懈，倒抽其斧，反斫之，突城而出，趨木華黎行營，求得蒙古軍數千，回與敵戰，敗之。

translations.literal: Watching for a moment when the enemy relaxed slightly, he snatched back their axe and struck back, burst out of the city, hurried to Muqali's field headquarters, obtained several thousand Mongol troops, returned to fight the enemy, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy slackened for a moment, he wrested an axe from them and struck back, broke out of the city, and raced to Muqali's camp. There he secured several thousand Mongol troops, returned to meet the foe, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 木華黎嘉其勇，奏授金符，行元帥；

translations.literal: Muqali praised his courage, memorialized to grant him a golden tally, and made him acting marshal;
translations.idiomatic: Muqali praised his valor, memorialized for a golden tally, and appointed him acting marshal;

sentences.zh: 尋詔將官各就本城，授興中府千戶。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered the officers each to their home city, and he was appointed chiliarch of Xingzhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict sent the officers back to their home cities, and Zuozhong was made chiliarch of Xingzhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 子安琬

translations.literal: His son Anwan
translations.idiomatic: Anwan

sentences.zh: 子安琬，襲職，佩金符，從征大理，討李璮，皆有功。

translations.literal: His son Anwan inherited the post, wore a golden tally, followed campaigns against Dali and against Li Tan, and distinguished himself in both.
translations.idiomatic: His son Anwan inherited the family post, wore the golden tally, and earned distinction in campaigns against Dali and in the suppression of Li Tan.

sentences.zh: 十三年，隆興之分寧叛，行省檄安琬討之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Fenning in Longxing rebelled, and the Branch Secretariat dispatched Anwan to suppress it.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, Fenning in Longxing rose in revolt, and the Branch Secretariat ordered Anwan to put it down.

sentences.zh: 賊背山而陣，安琬引兵出陣後，賊驚潰，退而距守。

translations.literal: The rebels drew up their battle line with the mountain at their backs. Anwan led troops behind their formation. The rebels panicked and routed, then withdrew to hold their position.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels formed their line with the mountain at their backs. Anwan swung his troops behind them; the rebels broke in panic and fell back to their fortifications.

sentences.zh: 安琬揮兵直抵壘門，賊揚言曰：「願少容行伍而戰，死且不憾。」

translations.literal: Anwan waved his troops straight to the rampart gate. The rebels proclaimed: "We ask only a little room to deploy our ranks and fight; even in death we shall have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: Anwan drove his men straight to the stockade gate. The rebels called out: "Give us room to deploy our ranks and fight—we will die without regret."

sentences.zh: 安琬從之，賊果出陣，安琬突陣而入，大呼曰：「吾止誅賊首，庸卒非我敵也。」

translations.literal: Anwan consented. The rebels indeed came out in formation. Anwan burst through the lines and cried aloud: "I seek only the rebel chiefs. Common soldiers are no match for me."
translations.idiomatic: Anwan agreed. The rebels came out to fight. He plunged through their ranks and shouted, "I want only the rebel leaders—common soldiers are not my concern!"

sentences.zh: 手刃中賊背，生擒之。

translations.literal: With his own hand he struck the rebel leader in the back and captured him alive.
translations.idiomatic: He struck the rebel chief in the back with his own blade and took him alive.

sentences.zh: 累功至右衛親軍副都指揮使，進階懷遠大將軍，賜金虎符，後授大同等處萬戶，領江左新附卒萬人，屯田紅城。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit he rose to deputy commander of the Right Imperial Guard, was promoted to Grand General of Cherishing the Distant, was granted a golden tiger tally, and was later appointed myriarch of Datong and other regions, commanding ten thousand newly submitted troops from the left bank of the Yangtze and farming garrison fields at Hongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Through repeated merit he rose to deputy commander of the Right Imperial Guard, was promoted to Grand General of Cherishing the Distant, and received a golden tiger tally. Later he was made myriarch of Datong and neighboring regions, commanding ten thousand newly submitted troops from south of the Yangtze at the Hongcheng garrison farms.

sentences.zh: 大德三年，李萬戶當戍和寧，親老且病，安琬請代其行，及還，以病卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dade, when Li the Myriad Household was due to garrison Hening, his parents were old and ill. Anwan volunteered to take his place. When he returned, he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dade, when Li the Myriad Household was scheduled to garrison Hening, his parents were old and ill. Anwan volunteered to go in his stead. He died of illness upon his return.

sentences.zh: 子居謙襲職，後改忠翊侍衛親軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: His son Juqian inherited the post and was later made commander of the Loyal Support Personal Guard of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Juqian inherited the post and was later appointed commander of the Loyal Support Personal Guard.

sentences.zh: 移剌捏兒

translations.literal: Yelü Nie'er
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Nie'er

sentences.zh: 移剌捏兒，契丹人也。

translations.literal: Yelü Nie'er was a Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Nie'er was a Khitan.

sentences.zh: 幼有大志，膂力過人，沉毅多謀略。

translations.literal: From youth he harbored great ambition, his physical strength surpassed other men, and he was deep, resolute, and rich in stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he burned with ambition. His strength surpassed other men's, and he was grave, resolute, and full of stratagem.

sentences.zh: 遼亡，金以為參議、留守等官，皆辭不受。

translations.literal: When Liao fell, the Jin appointed him to posts such as councilor and territorial commissioner, but he declined them all.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Liao, the Jin offered him posts such as councilor and territorial commissioner, but he refused them all.

sentences.zh: 聞太祖舉兵，私語所親曰：「為國復讎，此其時也。」

translations.literal: Hearing that the Taizu had raised troops, he privately told those close to him: "To avenge the state — this is the hour."
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Genghis Khan had taken up arms, he told those closest to him in private: "To avenge our country—this is the moment."

sentences.zh: 率其黨百餘人詣軍門獻十策。

translations.literal: He led more than a hundred of his followers to the army gate and presented ten stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: He led more than a hundred followers to the army gate and presented ten stratagems.

sentences.zh: 帝召見，與語奇之，賜名賽因必闍赤。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him for audience, found him remarkable in conversation, and granted him the name Sayin Bayichi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him, was struck by his speech, and granted him the name Sayin Bayichi.

sentences.zh: 又問：「爾生何地？」

translations.literal: He asked again: "Where were you born?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked again, "Where were you born?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「霸州。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Bazhou."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Bazhou."

sentences.zh: 因號為霸州元帥。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was styled Marshal of Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was styled the Marshal of Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，拜兵馬都元帥，佐太師木華黎取北京，下高、利、興、松、義、錦等二十六城，破五十四寨，平利州賊劉四祿。

translations.literal: In the yihai year he was appointed marshal of all troops and horses, assisted Grand Preceptor Muqali in taking Beiping, captured twenty-six cities including Gao, Li, Xing, Song, Yi, and Jin, broke fifty-four stockades, and pacified the Li Prefecture bandit Liu Silu.
translations.idiomatic: In the yihai year he was made marshal of all troops and horses and assisted Grand Preceptor Muqali in taking Beiping. He captured twenty-six cities—including Gao, Li, Xing, Song, Yi, and Jin—broke fifty-four stockades, and crushed the Li Prefecture rebel Liu Silu.

sentences.zh: 及錦州賊張致兵勢方熾，且盜名號，木華黎命捏兒與大將烏也兒、椆斡兒合兵討之。

translations.literal: When the Jin Prefecture bandit Zhang Zhi's army was at the height of its power and he had usurped titles, Muqali ordered Nie'er to join generals Uya'er and Chuo'guo'er in combined forces to subdue him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin Prefecture rebel Zhang Zhi's forces were at their peak and he had seized imperial titles for himself, Muqali ordered Nie'er to join generals Uya'er and Chuo'guo'er in a combined campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 致拒戰，捏兒出奇兵掩擊，斬致。

translations.literal: Zhi resisted battle. Nie'er sent out surprise troops in a flanking strike and beheaded Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi gave battle. Nie'er sent a surprise force in a flanking attack and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 木華黎第功以聞，遷龍虎衛上將軍、兵馬都提控元帥。

translations.literal: Muqali ranked their merits and reported upward. Nie'er was promoted to senior general of the Longhu Guard and marshal controller of all troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali ranked their merits and reported to the throne. Nie'er was promoted to senior general of the Longhu Guard and overall controller marshal of all troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 繼取遼東西廣寧、金、復、海、蓋等十五城。

translations.literal: He next took fifteen cities including Guangning, Jin, Fu, Hai, and Gai in eastern and western Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to capture fifteen cities in eastern and western Liaodong, including Guangning, Jin, Fu, Hai, and Gai.

sentences.zh: 興州監州重兒反，復與烏也兒討平之。

translations.literal: Chong'er, the Jin Prefecture commissioner of Xingzhou, rebelled. Again joining Uya'er, he suppressed and pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: Chong'er, the Jin Prefecture commissioner of Xingzhou, rebelled. Nie'er again joined Uya'er and put the revolt down.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使者詔之曰：「自汝效順，戰功日多，今錫汝金虎符，居則理民，有事則將，其勿替朕意。」

translations.literal: The emperor sent an envoy with an edict saying: "Since you submitted in loyalty, your battle achievements grow daily. Now I grant you a golden tiger tally: in peace administer the people, in crisis lead the armies. Do not fail my intent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an envoy with an edict: "Since you came over in loyalty, your battlefield achievements have only grown. I now grant you a golden tiger tally—in peace you shall govern the people, in war you shall lead the armies. Do not disappoint my trust."

sentences.zh: 戊寅，從攻東平。

translations.literal: In the wuyin year, he followed the attack on Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuyin year, he joined the assault on Dongping.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，從攻延安。

translations.literal: In the xinsi year, he followed the attack on Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinsi year, he joined the assault on Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 壬午，從圍鳳翔，先登，手殺數十人，左臂中流矢，創甚，裹創進攻丹、延。

translations.literal: In the renwu year, following the siege of Fengxiang, he was first to ascend the walls, killed several dozen men with his own hand, took an arrow in his left arm with a grievous wound, bound the wound and pressed the attack on Dan and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the renwu year, at the siege of Fengxiang, he was first over the wall and killed several dozen men with his own hand. An arrow struck his left arm—a grievous wound—but he bound it and pressed on against Dan and Yan.

sentences.zh: 木華黎止之，對曰：「創未至死，敢自愛耶！」

translations.literal: Muqali stopped him. He replied: "The wound has not yet reached death — how dare I spare myself!"
translations.idiomatic: Muqali tried to stop him. He replied, "This wound has not killed me yet—how dare I hold back!"

sentences.zh: 木華黎壯之，與所乘白馬。

translations.literal: Muqali admired him and gave him the white horse he himself rode.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali was moved by his spirit and gave him the white horse he himself rode.

sentences.zh: 明日，介其馬，飾以朱纓，簡驍衛七百人，與金兵戰。

translations.literal: The next day, he armored the horse, adorned it with red tassels, selected seven hundred fierce guards, and fought Jin troops.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he armored the horse, hung it with red tassels, picked seven hundred elite guards, and met the Jin in battle.

sentences.zh: 木華黎乘高，見其馳突萬衆中，曰：「此霸州元帥也。」

translations.literal: Muqali took a high vantage and saw him charging through ten thousand men, saying, "That is the Marshal of Bazhou."
translations.idiomatic: From a height Muqali watched him charge through the mass of enemy troops and said, "There goes the Marshal of Bazhou."

sentences.zh: 諸軍繼進，金兵敗走，丹、延十餘城皆降，遷軍民都達魯花赤、都提控元帥，兼興勝府尹。

translations.literal: The armies pressed forward in succession. Jin troops were defeated and fled. More than ten cities of Dan and Yan all submitted. He was promoted to chief darughachi of military and civil affairs, overall controller marshal, and concurrently prefect of Xingsheng.
translations.idiomatic: The armies pressed forward. The Jin broke and fled, and more than ten cities in Dan and Yan surrendered. He was promoted to chief darughachi of military and civil affairs, overall controller marshal, and concurrently prefect of Xingsheng.

sentences.zh: 癸未，從帝征河西，取甘、合、辛、蛇等州。

translations.literal: In the guiwei year, he followed the emperor's western campaign, taking Gan, He, Xin, She, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the guiwei year he followed the emperor's campaign into the Hexi region and captured Gan, He, Xin, She, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 師還，復從木華黎攻益都，下萊、膠、淄等三十二城。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he again followed Muqali in attacking Yidu, taking thirty-two cities including Lai, Jiao, and Zi.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he again followed Muqali against Yidu and captured thirty-two cities, including Lai, Jiao, and Zi.

sentences.zh: 戊子，得疾歸高州，卒。

translations.literal: In the wuzi year, he fell ill, returned to Gaozhou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuzi year he fell ill, returned to Gaozhou, and died.

sentences.zh: 贈推忠宣力保德功臣、太尉、開府儀同三司、上柱國，追封興國公，諡武毅。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Promotes Loyalty, Proclaims Strength, and Preserves Virtue, Grand Preceptor, Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Grand Marshal of the State, Upper Pillar of the State; was enfeoffed as Duke of Xing; and was given the posthumous name Martial Resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was honored as Meritorious Minister Who Promotes Loyalty, Proclaims Strength, and Preserves Virtue, with the ranks of Grand Preceptor, Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Grand Marshal of the State, and Upper Pillar of the State. He was enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Xing and given the temple name Martial Resolve.

sentences.zh: 子買奴。

translations.literal: His son Mainu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Mainu.

sentences.zh: 買奴，蚤從父習戰陣，初入見，太祖問曰：「汝年小，能襲父爵乎？」

translations.literal: Mainu from youth followed his father in learning battle formations. At his first audience upon entering, the Taizu asked: "You are young — can you inherit your father's fief?"
translations.idiomatic: Mainu had studied warfare under his father from boyhood. At his first audience the Taizu asked, "You are still young—can you inherit your father's rank?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣年雖小，國法不小。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Though I am young, the laws of the state are not small."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I may be young, but the laws of the state are not."

sentences.zh: 帝異其對，顧左右曰：「此兒甚肖乃父。」

translations.literal: The emperor was struck by his reply and turned to those beside him: "This boy greatly resembles his father."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was impressed and turned to his attendants. "This boy is very much his father's son."

sentences.zh: 以為高州等處達魯花赤，兼征行萬戶。

translations.literal: He was made darughachi of Gaozhou and other regions, and concurrently campaign mobile myriarch.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed darughachi of Gaozhou and neighboring regions, and concurrently campaign mobile myriarch.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，命攻高麗花涼城，監軍張翼、劉霸都殞於敵，買奴怒曰：「兩將陷賊，義不獨生！」

translations.literal: In the gengyin year, ordered to attack Hualiang City in Goryeo, supervising generals Zhang Yi and Liu Badu perished at the enemy's hands. Mainu raged: "Two generals lost to the enemy — righteousness forbids my living alone!"
translations.idiomatic: In the gengyin year, ordered to attack Hualiang City in Goryeo, he learned that supervising generals Zhang Yi and Liu Badu had fallen to the enemy. Mainu raged: "Two commanders lost—I cannot live on alone!"

sentences.zh: 趨出戰，破之，誅首將，撫安其民。

translations.literal: He rushed forth to battle, broke the enemy, executed the chief commander, and pacified the people.
translations.idiomatic: He charged into battle, broke the enemy, executed their commander, and restored order among the people.

sentences.zh: 進攻開州，州將金沙密逆戰，擒之，城中人出童男女及金玉器以獻，却不受。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Kaizhou, the prefectural commander Jin Shami resisted battle and was captured. The people of the city brought out boys and girls and gold and jade objects as tribute, but he refused them.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing on Kaizhou, he captured the prefectural commander Jin Shami after a hard fight. The townspeople offered boys and girls and gold and jade in tribute, but he refused them all.

sentences.zh: 遂下龍、宣、雲、泰等十四城。

translations.literal: He then took fourteen cities including Long, Xuan, Yun, and Tai.
translations.idiomatic: He then captured fourteen cities, including Long, Xuan, Yun, and Tai.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，從諸王按赤台征女直萬奴部，有功。

translations.literal: In the guisi year, he followed Prince Anchitai in campaigning against the Jurchen Wan Nu tribe and achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the guisi year he followed Prince Anchitai against the Jurchen chieftain Wan Nu and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 未幾召還。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 興州趙祚反，土豪楊買驢等附之。

translations.literal: Zhao Zuo of Xingzhou rebelled, and local magnates Yang Mailü and others joined him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zuo of Xingzhou rose in rebellion, and local magnates such as Yang Mailü rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 帝命從親王察合台帥師討之，斬賊將董蠻等，圍買驢於險樹寨，三月不能下。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to follow Prince Chagatai in leading troops to suppress them. They beheaded the rebel generals Dong Man and others, and besieged Mailü in Xianshu Stockade for three months without taking it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him to follow Prince Chagatai against the rebels. They beheaded rebel generals including Dong Man and besieged Mailü in Xianshu Stockade, but could not take it for three months.

sentences.zh: 買奴令健卒劉五兒，即寨北小徑上大樹，以繩潛引百人登寨，直前劫之，買驢投崖死，餘黨悉平。

translations.literal: Mainu ordered the stalwart soldier Liu Wu'er to climb a great tree on the small path north of the stockade, secretly draw up a hundred men by rope onto the ramparts, and strike straight forward in a raid. Mailü threw himself off the cliff and died, and the remaining factions were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Mainu ordered the stalwart Liu Wu'er to climb a great tree on the narrow path north of the stockade and secretly haul a hundred men up by rope onto the ramparts. They struck straight in. Mailü leapt from the cliff to his death, and the remaining rebels were all pacified.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，錄功，賜金鞍良馬。

translations.literal: When Taizong ascended the throne, his merits were recorded and he was given a golden saddle and fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Ögedei ascended the throne, Mainu's merits were recorded and he was rewarded with a golden saddle and fine horses.

sentences.zh: 乙未，從征高麗，入王京，取其西京而還，賜金鎖甲，加鎮國上將軍、征東大元帥，佩金符。

translations.literal: In the yiwei year, following the campaign against Goryeo, he entered the Royal Capital, took its Western Capital and returned. He was granted golden chain armor, promoted to State-pacifying Senior General and Grand Marshal for the Eastern Campaign, and wore a golden tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the yiwei year he joined the campaign against Goryeo, entered the royal capital, seized its Western Capital, and returned. He received golden chain armor, was promoted to State-pacifying Senior General and Grand Marshal for the Eastern Campaign, and was granted a golden tally.

sentences.zh: 復命出師高麗，將行，以疾卒，年四十。

translations.literal: Again ordered to lead troops against Goryeo, he was about to set out when he died of illness at age forty.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered once more to lead troops against Goryeo, he fell ill on the eve of departure and died at forty.

sentences.zh: 贈推誠效義功臣、榮祿大夫、平章政事，追封興國公，諡顯懿。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Promotes Sincerity and Proves Righteousness, Grand Master for Glorious Salary, and Grand Councillor; was enfeoffed as Duke of Xing; and was given the posthumous name Illustrious and Virtuous.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was honored as Meritorious Minister Who Promotes Sincerity and Proves Righteousness, with the ranks of Grand Master for Glorious Salary and Grand Councillor. He was enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Xing and given the temple name Illustrious and Virtuous.

sentences.zh: 子元臣。

translations.literal: His son Yuanchen.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yuanchen.

sentences.zh: 元臣，別名哈剌哈孫，年十六入宿衛，應對進止有度，世祖謂丞相和魯火孫曰：「此勳臣子，非凡器也。」

translations.literal: Yuanchen, also called Qaraqasun, entered the palace guard at sixteen. His bearing in response and in conduct had measure. Kublai said to Chancellor Arghun: "This is the son of a meritorious minister — no ordinary vessel."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchen, also called Qaraqasun, entered the palace guard at sixteen. In speech and bearing he showed uncommon poise. Kublai said to Chancellor Arghun, "This is the son of a meritorious minister—not an ordinary man."

sentences.zh: 以為怯薛必闍赤，襲千戶，將其父軍。

translations.literal: He was made keshik baurchi, inherited the chiliarchate, and commanded his father's army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a keshik baurchi, inherited the chiliarchate, and took command of his father's army.

sentences.zh: 從伐宋，攻淮西，戍清口，取瓜洲，下通、泰，累有功。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Song, he attacked west of the Huai, garrisoned Qingkou, took Guazhou, captured Tong and Tai, and repeatedly achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Song, fought west of the Huai, garrisoned Qingkou, took Guazhou, and captured Tong and Tai, earning repeated distinction.

sentences.zh: 至元十二年，從丞相伯顏平宋，進階武義將軍、中衛親軍緫管，佩金虎符。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhiyuan, following Chancellor Bayan in pacifying Song, he was promoted to Martial Righteousness General and chief commander of the Central Imperial Guard, wearing a golden tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Zhiyuan he followed Chancellor Bayan in the conquest of Song and was promoted to Martial Righteousness General and chief commander of the Central Imperial Guard, with a golden tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 十四年，只兒瓦台叛，圍應昌府，時皇女魯國公主在圍中。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Jirwatay rebelled and besieged Yingchang Prefecture. At the time the emperor's daughter, the Princess of Lu, was within the siege.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Jirwatay rebelled and besieged Yingchang Prefecture while the emperor's daughter, the Princess of Lu, was trapped inside.

sentences.zh: 元臣以所部軍馳擊，只兒瓦台敗走，追至魚兒濼，擒之，公主賜賚甚厚，奏請暫留元臣鎮應昌，以安反側。

translations.literal: Yuanchen with the troops under his command galloped to strike. Jirwatay was defeated and fled. Pursued to Yuer Lake, he was captured. The princess rewarded him richly and memorialized to retain Yuanchen temporarily to garrison Yingchang and pacify those inclined to revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchen galloped to the rescue with his troops. Jirwatay was routed and fled; Yuanchen pursued him to Yuer Lake and captured him. The princess rewarded him lavishly and petitioned to keep him at Yingchang to calm the restless region.

sentences.zh: 居一歲，召至京師，遷明威將軍、後衛親軍副都指揮使，還鎮應昌。

translations.literal: After one year he was summoned to the capital, promoted to Bright Martial General and deputy commander of the Rear Imperial Guard, and returned to garrison Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was summoned to the capital, promoted to Bright Martial General and deputy commander of the Rear Imperial Guard, and sent back to garrison Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 又三歲，召還，加昭勇大將軍。

translations.literal: After three more years he was recalled and promoted to Illustrious Valor Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he was recalled again and promoted to Illustrious Valor Grand General.

sentences.zh: 十九年，帝以所籍入權臣家婦賜之，元臣辭曰：「臣家世清素，不敢自污。」

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, the emperor wished to grant him a woman confiscated from a powerful minister's household. Yuanchen declined: "My family has been pure and plain for generations — I dare not defile myself."
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the emperor wished to grant him a woman confiscated from a powerful minister's household. Yuanchen declined: "My family has lived in plain honesty for generations—I dare not stain myself."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉嘆不已。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and sighed without end.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him again and again.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，進昭毅大將軍，同僉江淮行樞密院事；

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, he was promoted to Illustrious Resolve Grand General and associate envoy of the Jianghuai Branch Privy Council;
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to Illustrious Resolve Grand General and made associate envoy of the Jianghuai Branch Privy Council;

sentences.zh: 行院罷，歸高州。

translations.literal: When the branch council was abolished, he returned to Gaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the branch council was abolished, he returned to Gaozhou.

sentences.zh: 帝親征乃顏，元臣率家僮五十人見行在所，願效前驅。

translations.literal: When the emperor personally campaigned against Nayan, Yuanchen led fifty household retainers to the mobile palace and volunteered to serve as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai personally marched against Nayan, Yuanchen brought fifty household retainers to the imperial camp and offered to serve as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 八年，移僉湖廣行樞密院，時溪洞施、容等州蠻獠作亂，元臣親入其境，喻以禍福，賊首魯萬丑降。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was transferred as associate envoy of the Huguang Branch Privy Council. At the time the Man and Liao of the stream-cave prefectures Shi, Rong, and others rebelled. Yuanchen personally entered their territory, explained fortune and disaster to them, and the bandit chief Lu Wanchou submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to the Huguang Branch Privy Council as associate envoy. When the tribal peoples of the stream-cave prefectures Shi, Rong, and others rose in revolt, Yuanchen entered their lands in person, spoke to them of reward and ruin, and the rebel chief Lu Wanchou surrendered.

sentences.zh: 三十年，卒于官。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈安遠功臣、龍虎衛上將軍、同知樞密院事，追封興國公，諡忠靖。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Pacifies the Distant, senior general of the Longhu Guard, and vice-director of the Privy Council; was enfeoffed as Duke of Xing; and was given the posthumous name Loyal and Tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was honored as Meritorious Minister Who Pacifies the Distant, with the ranks of senior general of the Longhu Guard and vice-director of the Privy Council. He was enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Xing and given the temple name Loyal and Tranquil.

sentences.zh: 子迪，中奉大夫、湖廣宣慰使都元帥。

translations.literal: His son Di, Grand Master for Glorious Acceptance, commander-in-chief and pacification commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Di served as Grand Master for Glorious Acceptance and commander-in-chief and pacification commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 耶律禿花

translations.literal: Yelu Tuhua
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Tuhua

sentences.zh: 耶律禿花，契丹人。

translations.literal: Yelu Tuhua was a Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Tuhua was a Khitan.

sentences.zh: 世居桓州，太祖時，率衆來歸。

translations.literal: For generations he had lived at Huanzhou; in the time of Taizu he led his followers to submit.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long lived at Huanzhou; in the time of Taizu he led his people to come over.

sentences.zh: 大軍入金境，為嚮導，獲所牧馬甚衆。

translations.literal: When the great army entered Jin territory, he served as guide and captured a very great number of horses from the pastures.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army entered Jin territory, he served as guide and captured a great many horses from the enemy pastures.

sentences.zh: 後侍太祖，同飲班朮河水。

translations.literal: Later he attended Taizu and drank together from the waters of the Banzhu River.
translations.idiomatic: Later he attended Taizu and drank with him from the Banzhu River.

sentences.zh: 從伐金，大破忽察虎軍。

translations.literal: He followed in the campaign against Jin and routed Huchahu's army.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaign against Jin and routed the army of Huchahu.

sentences.zh: 又從木華黎收山東、河北，有功，拜太傅、緫領也可那延，封濮國公，賜虎符、銀印，歲給錦幣三百六十匹。

translations.literal: He also followed Muqali in pacifying Shandong and Hebei; for his achievements he was appointed Grand Tutor and commander-in-chief yeke nayan, enfeoffed as Duke of Pu, granted a tiger tally and silver seal, and given three hundred and sixty bolts of brocade annually.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed Muqali in pacifying Shandong and Hebei. For his achievements he was made Grand Tutor and yeke nayan commander-in-chief, enfeoffed as Duke of Pu, granted a tiger tally and silver seal, and given three hundred and sixty bolts of brocade each year.

sentences.zh: 統萬戶扎剌兒、劉黑馬、史天澤伐金，卒于西河州。

translations.literal: Commanding the ten-thousand-household units of the Jala'ir, Liu Heima, and Shi Tianze, he campaigned against Jin and died at Xihe Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Commanding the Jala'ir, Liu Heima, and Shi Tianze ten-thousand-household units, he campaigned against Jin and died at Xihe Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 子朱哥嗣，仍統劉黑馬等七萬戶，與都元帥塔海紺卜同征四川，卒于軍。

translations.literal: His son Zhuge succeeded him, still commanding the seventy thousand households of Liu Heima and others; campaigning against Sichuan together with the commander-in-chief Tachar Keben, he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhuge succeeded him and still commanded the seventy thousand households of Liu Heima and others. Campaigning against Sichuan with the commander-in-chief Tachar Keben, he died in the field.

sentences.zh: 子寶童嗣，以疾不任事。

translations.literal: His son Baotong succeeded but, owing to illness, could not perform his duties.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baotong succeeded him but, owing to illness, could not carry out his duties.

sentences.zh: 朱哥弟買住嗣，而以寶童充隨路新軍緫管。

translations.literal: Zhuge's younger brother Maizhu succeeded, while Baotong was appointed overall commander of the new armies along the routes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge's younger brother Maizhu succeeded him, while Baotong was appointed overall commander of the new armies along the routes.

sentences.zh: 買住言於憲宗曰：「今欲略定西川下流諸城，當先定成都，以為根本，臣請往相其地。」

translations.literal: Maizhu said to Emperor Xianzong: "If we now wish to pacify the downstream cities of western Sichuan, we should first secure Chengdu as our base. Your subject requests permission to go and survey the site."
translations.idiomatic: Maizhu said to Emperor Xianzong: "If we mean to pacify the downstream cities of western Sichuan, we must first secure Chengdu as our base. I ask leave to go and survey the ground."

sentences.zh: 帝從之，遂率諸軍往成都，攻嘉定，未下而卒。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed. He then led the armies to Chengdu and attacked Jiading, but died before the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed. He then led the armies to Chengdu and attacked Jiading, but died before the city was taken.

sentences.zh: 子忽林帶嗣，緫諸軍，立成都府，卒于軍。

translations.literal: His son Hulindai succeeded, commanded the armies, established Chengdu Prefecture, and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hulindai succeeded him, took command of the armies, established Chengdu Prefecture, and died in the field.

sentences.zh: 以兄百家奴嗣。

translations.literal: His elder brother Baijianu succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Baijianu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 自朱哥至百家奴，並襲太傅、緫領也可那延。

translations.literal: From Zhuge to Baijianu, all inherited the titles Grand Tutor and commander-in-chief yeke nayan.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhuge down to Baijianu, each in turn inherited the posts of Grand Tutor and yeke nayan commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 買住子禿滿荅兒

translations.literal: Maizhu's son Tumandai'er
translations.idiomatic: Maizhu's son Tumandai'er

sentences.zh: 禿滿荅兒者，百家奴之弟，忽林帶之兄也，常留中宿衛。

translations.literal: Tumandai'er was Baijianu's younger brother and Hulindai's elder brother, and was often kept at court as an imperial guard.
translations.idiomatic: Tumandai'er was Baijianu's younger brother and Hulindai's elder brother, and was often kept at court on palace guard duty.

sentences.zh: 後百家奴解兵柄為他官，乃授成都管軍萬戶，代將其軍。

translations.literal: Later, when Baijianu relinquished military command for another post, Tumandai'er was appointed commander of the Chengdu garrison ten-thousand-household unit and took command of the army in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Baijianu gave up military command for another post, Tumandai'er was appointed commander of the Chengdu garrison ten-thousand-household unit and took over his army.

sentences.zh: 至元十一年，從忽敦攻嘉定，修平康寨以守之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhiyuan he followed Hudun in attacking Jiading and built and held Pingkang Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Zhiyuan (1274) he followed Hudun in attacking Jiading, built Pingkang Stockade, and held it.

sentences.zh: 十二年，從汪田哥攻九頂山，破之，殺都統一人，嘉定降。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he followed Wang Tiange in attacking Jiuding Mountain, broke it, killed one commander-in-chief, and Jiading surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he followed Wang Tiange in attacking Jiuding Mountain, broke the position, killed a commander-in-chief, and Jiading surrendered.

sentences.zh: 從忽敦徇下瀘、敘諸城，圍重慶，守合江口，又以舟師塞龍門濠，遏其援兵。

translations.literal: He followed Hudun in subduing the cities downstream of Lu and Xu, besieged Chongqing, held Hejiang Mouth, and with a fleet blocked Longmen Moat to cut off relief troops.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Hudun in subduing the cities downstream of Lu and Xu, besieged Chongqing, held Hejiang Mouth, and used his fleet to block Longmen Moat and cut off enemy relief.

sentences.zh: 十三年，瀘州叛，從汪田哥攻之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Luzhou rebelled, and he followed Wang Tiange in attacking it.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Luzhou rebelled, and he followed Wang Tiange to attack it.

sentences.zh: 重慶遣兵援瀘，邀擊破之，獲七十人。

translations.literal: Chongqing sent troops to relieve Luzhou; he intercepted and defeated them, capturing seventy men.
translations.idiomatic: Chongqing sent troops to relieve Luzhou; he intercepted them, won the fight, and took seventy prisoners.

sentences.zh: 瀘堅守不下，禿滿荅兒夜率兵，攻奪水城以進，黎明，先登，入瀘城，克之，斬其將王世昌、李都統。

translations.literal: Luzhou held firm and would not fall. Tumandai'er led troops by night, seized Shuicheng to advance, and at dawn was first to scale the wall and enter Luzhou; the city was taken and its generals Wang Shichang and Commander Li were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Luzhou held out stubbornly. Tumandai'er led a night attack, seized Shuicheng to press forward, and at dawn was first over the wall into Luzhou. The city fell, and its generals Wang Shichang and Commander Li were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 復從不花圍重慶，守將張珏搏戰，敗之城下，重慶降。

translations.literal: He again followed Buhua in besieging Chongqing; the defending commander Zhang Jue fought fiercely, was defeated beneath the walls, and Chongqing surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Buhua in besieging Chongqing. The defending commander Zhang Jue fought fiercely but was defeated beneath the walls, and Chongqing surrendered.

sentences.zh: 賜虎符，授夔路招討使，遷四川東道宣慰使，仍兼夔路招討，改同僉四川等處行樞密院事，遷四川等處行中書省左丞。

translations.literal: He was granted a tiger tally and appointed pacification commissioner of the Kuizhou circuit; promoted to pacification commissioner of the eastern Sichuan circuit while retaining the Kuizhou pacification post; made associate administrator of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat for Military Affairs; and promoted to Left Vice Administrator of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a tiger tally and appointed pacification commissioner of the Kuizhou circuit, then promoted to pacification commissioner of eastern Sichuan while retaining the Kuizhou post. He became associate administrator of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat for Military Affairs and was then promoted to Left Vice Administrator of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尚書省立，改行尚書省左丞，進右丞，卒。

translations.literal: When the Ministry of Revenue was established, he was transferred to Left Vice Administrator of the Branch Ministry, promoted to Right Vice Administrator, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Revenue was established, he was made Left Vice Administrator of the Branch Ministry, promoted to Right Vice Administrator, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 寶童子忙古帶

translations.literal: Baotong's son Mangudai
translations.idiomatic: Baotong's son Mangudai

sentences.zh: 忙古帶，寶童之子也。

translations.literal: Mangudai was Baotong's son.
translations.idiomatic: Mangudai was Baotong's son.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，賜金符，襲父職，為隨路新軍緫管，統領山西兩路新軍。

translations.literal: Under Shizu he was granted a golden tally, inherited his father's post as overall commander of the new armies along the routes, and commanded the new armies of the two circuits of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kublai he was granted a golden tally, inherited his father's post as overall commander of the new armies along the routes, and took charge of the new armies of the two Shanxi circuits.

sentences.zh: 從行省也速帶兒征蜀及思、播、建都諸蠻夷，有功，陞萬戶。

translations.literal: He followed the Regional Secretariat's Yesudai'er in campaigning in Shu and against the barbarian peoples of Si, Bo, and Jiandu, and for his achievements was promoted to commander of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the regional commissioner Yesudai'er in campaigns in Shu and against the Si, Bo, and Jiandu tribes, and for his achievements was promoted to commander of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 從攻羅必甸，至雲南，詔以其衆入緬，迎雲南王。

translations.literal: He followed the attack on Luobidian, reached Yunnan, and by imperial order led his troops into Burma to receive the Prince of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the attack on Luobidian, reached Yunnan, and by imperial order led his troops into Burma to escort the Prince of Yunnan back.

sentences.zh: 金齒、白衣、荅奔諸蠻，往往伏險要為備，忙古帶奮擊破之，凡十餘戰，至緬境，開金齒道，奉王以還，遷副都元帥。

translations.literal: The barbarians of Jinchí, Baiyi, and Daben often lay in ambush at strategic passes; Mangudai fought fiercely and broke them in more than ten battles, reached the Burmese frontier, opened the Jinchí road, escorted the prince back, and was promoted to deputy commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Jinchí, Baiyi, and Daben tribes often lay in ambush at strategic passes. Mangudai fought through them in more than ten battles, reached the Burmese frontier, opened the Jinchí road, escorted the prince home, and was promoted to deputy commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 從諸王阿台征交趾，至白鶴江，與交趾偽昭文王戰，奪其戰艦八十七艘。

translations.literal: He followed Prince Atai in campaigning against Annam, reached Baihe River, fought the false King Zhaowen of Annam, and captured eighty-seven warships.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince Atai in the campaign against Annam, reached the Baihe River, fought the self-styled King Zhaowen of Annam, and captured eighty-seven warships.

sentences.zh: 又從雲南王攻羅必甸，破之。

translations.literal: He again followed the Prince of Yunnan in attacking Luobidian and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the Prince of Yunnan in attacking Luobidian and defeated it.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，入覲。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he came to court for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he came to court for an audience.

sentences.zh: 王珣字君寶，本姓耶律氏，世為遼大族。

translations.literal: Wang Xun, courtesy name Junbao, was originally surnamed Yelü and for generations had been a great clan of Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun, courtesy name Junbao, was originally of the Yelü clan and for generations had been one of Liao's great families.

sentences.zh: 金正隆末，契丹窩斡叛，祖成，從母氏避難遼西，更姓王氏，遂為義州開義人。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jin Zhenglong era, when the Khitan Wohuo rebelled, his grandfather Cheng fled with his mother's clan to western Liao, changed his surname to Wang, and became a native of Kaiyi in Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jin Zhenglong era, when the Khitan Wohuo rebelled, his grandfather Cheng fled with his mother's people to western Liao, changed his surname to Wang, and became a native of Kaiyi in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 父伯俊。

translations.literal: His father was Bojun.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Bojun.

sentences.zh: 伯父伯亨無子，以珣為後。

translations.literal: His uncle Boheng had no son and adopted Xun as his heir.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Boheng had no son and adopted Xun as his heir.

sentences.zh: 珣武力絕人，善騎射，尤長於擊鞠。

translations.literal: Xun's martial prowess was unmatched; he excelled at mounted archery and was especially skilled at cuju.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's martial prowess was unmatched. He excelled at mounted archery and was especially skilled at cuju.

sentences.zh: 年三十餘，遇道士，謂珣曰：「君之相甚奇，它日因一青馬而貴。」

translations.literal: When he was over thirty he met a Daoist who said to Xun: "Your countenance is most extraordinary; one day you will rise to eminence because of a blue horse."
translations.idiomatic: When he was over thirty he met a Daoist who said to Xun: "Your face is most extraordinary. One day you will rise to eminence because of a blue horse."

sentences.zh: 珣未之信。

translations.literal: Xun did not believe him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun did not believe him.

sentences.zh: 居歲餘，有客以青馬來鬻，珣私喜曰：「道士之言或驗乎？」

translations.literal: After more than a year a traveler came to sell a blue horse. Xun said to himself with quiet delight: "Might the Daoist's words prove true?"
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year a traveler came to sell a blue horse. Xun said to himself with quiet delight: "Could the Daoist's words be coming true?"

sentences.zh: 乃倍價買之，後乘以戰，其進退周旋，無不如意。

translations.literal: He bought it at double the price. Later, riding it in battle, every advance, retreat, and maneuver went exactly as he wished.
translations.idiomatic: He bought it at double the price. Later, riding it in battle, every advance, retreat, and maneuver went exactly as he wished.

sentences.zh: 又嘗行凌水濱，得一古刀，其背銘曰：「舉無不克，動必成功。」

translations.literal: Once, walking along the banks of the Ling River, he found an ancient blade; on its back was an inscription: "Raise it and nothing is not conquered; act and success is assured."
translations.idiomatic: Once, walking along the Ling River, he found an ancient blade. On its back was an inscription: "Raise it and nothing fails to fall; act and success is assured."

sentences.zh: 常佩之，每有警，必先鳴，故所向皆捷。

translations.literal: He wore it constantly. Whenever danger was near it would ring first, and so wherever he went he prevailed.
