translations.idiomatic: He wore it constantly. Whenever danger was near it would ring first, and so wherever he went he prevailed.

sentences.zh: 初，河朔兵動，豪強各擁衆據地，珣慨然曰：「世故如此，大丈夫當自振拔，否則為人所制。」

translations.literal: At first, when turmoil broke out in the north of the Yellow River, powerful locals each raised bands and seized territory. Xun said with feeling: "Affairs have come to this; a true man ought to lift himself up, or else he will be mastered by others."
translations.idiomatic: At first, when turmoil broke out north of the Yellow River, local strongmen each raised bands and seized territory. Xun said with feeling: "Affairs have come to this. A true man must lift himself up, or else others will master him."

sentences.zh: 乃召諸鄉人，諭以保親族之計，衆從之，推珣為長，旬月之間，招集遺民至十餘萬。

translations.literal: He summoned the people of his district, explained a plan to protect their kinsmen, and they agreed, making Xun their leader. Within a month he had gathered more than a hundred thousand displaced people.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the people of his district, explained a plan to protect their kinsmen, and they agreed to make Xun their leader. Within a month he had gathered more than a hundred thousand displaced people.

sentences.zh: 歲乙亥，太師木華黎略地奚霫，珣率吏民出迎，承制以珣為元帥，兼領義、川二州事。

translations.literal: In the year yihai, Grand Preceptor Muqali pacified the lands of the Xi tribe; Xun led officials and people out to welcome him and, by provisional appointment, was made marshal and put in charge of both Yizhou and Chuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In yihai (1215), Grand Preceptor Muqali pacified the Xi lands. Xun led officials and people out to welcome him and, by provisional appointment, was made marshal with charge of both Yizhou and Chuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙子春，張致僭號錦州，陰結開義楊伯傑等來掠義州，珣出戰，伯傑引去。

translations.literal: In the spring of the bingzi year, Zhang Zhi declared himself ruler at Jinzhou and secretly joined with Kaiyi's Yang Bojie and others to raid Yizhou. Xun went out to fight and Bojie withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of bingzi (1216), Zhang Zhi declared himself ruler at Jinzhou and secretly joined with Kaiyi's Yang Bojie and others to raid Yizhou. Xun went out to fight and Bojie withdrew.

sentences.zh: 會致兄子以千騎來衝，珣選十八騎突其前，復令左右掎角之，一卒以鎗刺珣，珣揮刀殺之，其衆潰走，獲其馬幾盡。

translations.literal: Just then Zhang Zhi's nephew came with a thousand horsemen to charge them. Xun chose eighteen riders to burst upon their van, then ordered flankers to pincer them. One soldier thrust a spear at Xun; Xun swung his blade and killed him, the enemy force broke and fled, and nearly all their horses were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Zhang Zhi's nephew came with a thousand horsemen to charge them. Xun chose eighteen riders to burst upon their van and ordered flankers to pincer them. One soldier thrust a spear at Xun; Xun swung his blade and killed him. The enemy broke and fled, and nearly all their horses were captured.

sentences.zh: 時興中亦叛，木華黎圍之，召珣以全軍來會，致窺覘其虛，夜襲之，家人皆遇害。

translations.literal: At that time Xingzhong also rebelled; Muqali besieged it and summoned Xun with his full army to join him. Zhang Zhi spied out his undefended home and raided it by night; Xun's family were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xingzhong also rebelled. Muqali besieged it and summoned Xun with his full army to join him. Zhang Zhi spied out his undefended home and raided it by night, and Xun's family were all killed.

sentences.zh: 及興中平，珣無所歸，木華黎留之興中，遣其子榮祖馳奏其事，帝諭之曰：「汝父子宣力我家，不意為張致所襲。

translations.literal: When Xingzhong was pacified, Xun had nowhere to return. Muqali kept him at Xingzhong and sent his son Rongzu at full gallop to report the matter. The emperor instructed him: "Your father and you have served our house with distinction; I did not expect you to be struck by Zhang Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingzhong was pacified, Xun had nowhere to return. Muqali kept him at Xingzhong and sent his son Rongzu at full gallop to report what had happened. The emperor told him: "Your father and you have served our house with distinction. I did not expect you to be struck down by Zhang Zhi.

sentences.zh: 歸語汝父，善撫其軍，自今以往，當忍恥蓄銳，俟逆黨平，彼之族屬、城邑、人民，一以付汝，吾不吝也。

translations.literal: Go tell your father to treat his troops well. From now on he should swallow his shame and sharpen his edge. When the rebel faction is crushed, their clans, cities, and people I shall wholly entrust to you—I shall not begrudge them.
translations.idiomatic: Go tell your father to treat his troops well. From now on he must swallow his shame and sharpen his edge. When the rebel faction is crushed, I shall entrust their clans, cities, and people wholly to you—I shall not begrudge them.

sentences.zh: 仍免徭賦五年，使汝父子世為大官。」

translations.literal: He was also exempted from corvée and taxes for five years, so that he and his father might hold high office for generations."
translations.idiomatic: He was also exempted from corvée and taxes for five years, so that he and his father might hold high office for generations."

sentences.zh: 珣以木華黎兵復開義，擒伯傑等，殺之。

translations.literal: With Muqali's troops Xun recovered Kaiyi, captured Bojie and the others, and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: With Muqali's troops Xun recovered Kaiyi, captured Bojie and the others, and executed them.

sentences.zh: 進攻錦州，致部將高益，縛致妻子及其黨千餘人以獻，木華黎悉以付珣，珣但誅致家，其餘皆釋之，始還義州。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Jinzhou, Zhang Zhi's subordinate general Gao Yi bound Zhang Zhi's wife and children and more than a thousand of his followers and surrendered them. Muqali turned them all over to Xun; Xun executed only Zhang Zhi's household and released the rest, then returned to Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to attack Jinzhou, Zhang Zhi's subordinate Gao Yi bound Zhang Zhi's wife and children and more than a thousand of his followers and surrendered them. Muqali turned them all over to Xun. Xun executed only Zhang Zhi's household, released the rest, and returned to Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，入朝，帝嘉其功，賜金虎符，加金紫光祿大夫、兵馬都元帥，鎮遼東便宜行事，兼義、川等州節度使。

translations.literal: In the dingchou year he came to court. The emperor praised his achievements, granted him a golden tiger tally, added the title Grand Master of Golden Purple Glory, made him commander-in-chief of horse and foot, gave him discretionary authority to pacify Liaodong, and appointed him military commissioner of Yizhou, Chuanzhou, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In dingchou (1217) he came to court. The emperor praised his achievements, granted him a golden tiger tally, made him Grand Master of Golden Purple Glory and commander-in-chief of horse and foot, gave him discretionary authority to pacify Liaodong, and appointed him military commissioner of Yizhou, Chuanzhou, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 珣貌黑，人呼為哈剌元帥，哈剌，中國言黑也。

translations.literal: Xun's complexion was dark; people called him the Kara Marshal—kara being the word for "black" in the language of China.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's complexion was dark, and people called him the Kara Marshal—kara meaning "black" in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 從木華黎兵略山東，至滿城，令還鎮，戒之曰：「彼新附之民，恃山海之險，反覆不常，非盡坑之，終必為變。」

translations.literal: He followed Muqali's army in pacifying Shandong as far as Mancheng. Muqali ordered him back to his post and warned him: "Those newly submitted people rely on mountains and sea for protection and are ever changeable. Unless they are wholly exterminated, they will surely rebel in the end."
translations.idiomatic: He followed Muqali's army in pacifying Shandong as far as Mancheng. Muqali ordered him back to his post and warned him: "Those newly submitted people rely on mountains and sea for protection and are ever changeable. Unless they are wholly exterminated, they will surely rebel in the end."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「國朝經略中夏，宜以恩信結人，若降者則殺，後寧復有至者乎！」

translations.literal: He replied: "In extending the dynasty's sway over central China, one ought to win people by grace and good faith. If those who surrender are killed, who afterward would ever come over?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "In extending the dynasty's sway over central China, one ought to win people by grace and good faith. If those who surrender are killed, who afterward would ever come over?"

sentences.zh: 遂還，以子榮祖代領其衆。

translations.literal: He then returned and had his son Rongzu take command of his forces in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned and had his son Rongzu take command of his forces in his stead.

sentences.zh: 甲申春正月卒，年四十八。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the jiashen year he died, aged forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in jiashen (1224) he died, aged forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 珣為政簡易，賞罰明信，誅強撫弱，毫髮無徇。

translations.literal: In governing, Xun was plain and uncomplicated; rewards and punishments were clear and trustworthy; he punished the strong and comforted the weak, without the slightest partiality.
translations.idiomatic: In governing, Xun was plain and direct. Rewards and punishments were clear and trustworthy; he punished the strong and comforted the weak, without the slightest partiality.

sentences.zh: 子四人，榮祖襲。

translations.literal: He had four sons; Rongzu succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons; Rongzu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 子榮祖

translations.literal: His son Rongzu
translations.idiomatic: His son Rongzu

sentences.zh: 榮祖字敬先，珣長子也。

translations.literal: Rongzu, courtesy name Jingxian, was Xun's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Rongzu, courtesy name Jingxian, was Xun's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 性沉厚，語音如鐘，勇力絕人。

translations.literal: By nature he was steady and grave; his voice rang like a bell; his courage and strength were unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was steady and grave. His voice rang like a bell, and his courage and strength were unmatched.

sentences.zh: 珣初附於木華黎，以榮祖為質，稍見任用。

translations.literal: When Xun first submitted to Muqali, he gave Rongzu as a hostage and Rongzu gradually won trust and employment.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun first submitted to Muqali, he gave Rongzu as a hostage, and Rongzu gradually won trust and employment.

sentences.zh: 珣卒，襲榮祿大夫、崇義軍節度使、義州管內觀察使。

translations.literal: When Xun died, Rongzu inherited the posts of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, military commissioner of the Chongyi Army, and surveillance commissioner within Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun died, Rongzu inherited the posts of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, military commissioner of the Chongyi Army, and surveillance commissioner within Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 從嗣國王孛魯入朝，帝聞其勇，選力士三人迭與之搏，皆應手而倒。

translations.literal: He followed the heir to the princely title Belu to court. The emperor, hearing of his bravery, chose three strongmen to wrestle with him in turn; each was knocked down at once.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the heir to the princely title Belu to court. The emperor, hearing of his bravery, chose three strongmen to wrestle with him in turn, and each was knocked down at once.

sentences.zh: 欲留置宿衛，會金平章政事葛不哥行省於遼東，咸平路宣撫使蒲鮮萬奴僭號於開元，遂命榮祖還，副撒里台進討之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to keep him as an imperial guard, but just then the Jin grand councilor Gebu Ge was conducting regional administration in Liaodong and Puxian Wannu, pacification commissioner of Xianping Circuit, had usurped the title at Kaiyuan. Rongzu was ordered back to serve as deputy to Saritai in advancing against him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to keep him as an imperial guard, but just then the Jin grand councilor Gebu Ge was administering Liaodong and Puxian Wannu, pacification commissioner of Xianping Circuit, had usurped the title at Kaiyuan. Rongzu was ordered back to serve as Saritai's deputy in advancing against him.

sentences.zh: 拔蓋州、宣城等十餘城，葛不哥走死。

translations.literal: They captured Gaizhou, Xuancheng, and more than ten other cities; Gebu Ge fled and died.
translations.idiomatic: They captured Gaizhou, Xuancheng, and more than ten other cities. Gebu Ge fled and died.

sentences.zh: 金帥郭琛、完顏曳魯馬、趙遵、李高奴等猶據石城，復攻拔之，曳魯馬戰死，遵與高奴出降。

translations.literal: The Jin commanders Guo Chen, Wanyan Yeluma, Zhao Zun, and Li Gaonu still held Shicheng; they attacked and took it again. Yeluma died in battle; Zun and Gaonu came out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin commanders Guo Chen, Wanyan Yeluma, Zhao Zun, and Li Gaonu still held Shicheng. They attacked and took it again. Yeluma died in battle; Zun and Gaonu came out and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 虜生口千餘，撒里台欲散於麾下，榮祖屢請，皆放為民。

translations.literal: More than a thousand captives were taken. Saritai wished to distribute them among his officers, but Rongzu repeatedly petitioned and they were all released to live as civilians.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand captives were taken. Saritai wished to distribute them among his officers, but Rongzu repeatedly petitioned and they were all released to live as civilians.

sentences.zh: 方城未下時，榮祖遣部卒賈實穴其城，城崩被壓，衆謂已死，弗顧也。

translations.literal: While Fangcheng had not yet fallen, Rongzu sent a subordinate, Jia Shi, to undermine the wall. The wall collapsed and buried him; the troops thought him dead and would not go to him.
translations.idiomatic: While Fangcheng had not yet fallen, Rongzu sent a subordinate, Jia Shi, to undermine the wall. The wall collapsed and buried him. The troops thought him dead and would not go to him.

sentences.zh: 榮祖曰：「士忘身死國，安忍棄去。」

translations.literal: Rongzu said: "This man forgot himself and died for the state—how could I bear to abandon him?"
translations.idiomatic: Rongzu said: "This man forgot himself and died for the state—how could I bear to abandon him?"

sentences.zh: 發石取之，猶生，一軍感激，樂為效死。

translations.literal: They dug away the stones and brought him out; he was still alive. The whole army was moved and gladly willing to die in service.
translations.idiomatic: They dug away the stones and brought him out; he was still alive. The whole army was moved and gladly willing to die in his service.

sentences.zh: 有言義人懷反側者，撒里台將屠之，榮祖馳驛奏辨，事乃止。

translations.literal: When someone reported that the people of Yi were disloyal, Saritai was about to massacre them. Rongzu raced post-horses to court to plead their case, and the matter was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When someone reported that the people of Yi were disloyal, Saritai was about to massacre them. Rongzu raced post-horses to court to plead their case, and the massacre was stopped.

sentences.zh: 己丑，授北京等路征行萬戶，換金虎符。

translations.literal: In the jichou year he was appointed campaign commander of the ten-thousand-household unit of the Beijing circuit and other routes, and was given a new golden tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: In jichou (1229) he was appointed campaign commander of the ten-thousand-household unit of the Beijing circuit and other routes and was given a new golden tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 伐高麗，圍其王京，高麗王力屈，遣其兄淮安公奉表納貢。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Goryeo, he besieged the royal capital; the Goryeo king's strength broke and he sent his elder brother the Duke of Huai'an with a memorial offering tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Goryeo, he besieged the royal capital. The Goryeo king's strength broke, and he sent his elder brother the Duke of Huai'an with a memorial offering tribute.

sentences.zh: 進討萬奴，擒之。

translations.literal: Advancing against Wannu, he captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing against Wannu, he captured him.

sentences.zh: 趙祁以興州叛，從諸王按只台平之。

translations.literal: Zhao Qi rebelled at Xingzhou; he followed Prince Anjitai in pacifying it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qi rebelled at Xingzhou, and he followed Prince Anjitai in pacifying it.

sentences.zh: 祁黨猶剽掠景、薊間，復從大將唐兀台討之，將行，榮祖曰：「承詔討逆人耳，豈可戮及無辜，宜惟抗我者誅。」

translations.literal: Qi's followers still raided between Jing and Ji. He again followed the great general Tangwutai to suppress them. Before they set out, Rongzu said: "We have received orders to punish rebels—how can we slaughter the innocent? Only those who resist us should be put to death."
translations.idiomatic: Qi's followers still raided between Jing and Ji. He again followed the great general Tangwutai to suppress them. Before they set out, Rongzu said: "We have received orders to punish rebels—how can we slaughter the innocent? Only those who resist us should be put to death."

sentences.zh: 大將然之，由是免死者衆。

translations.literal: The general agreed, and so many were spared death.
translations.idiomatic: The general agreed, and so many were spared death.

sentences.zh: 再從征高麗，破十餘城，高麗遣子綧入質。

translations.literal: He again followed a campaign against Goryeo, broke more than ten cities, and Goryeo sent the prince Chŏng as a hostage.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed a campaign against Goryeo, broke more than ten cities, and Goryeo sent Prince Chŏng as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 帝賜錦衣，旌其功。

translations.literal: The emperor granted him brocade robes in recognition of his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him brocade robes in recognition of his achievements.

sentences.zh: 又從諸王也忽略地三韓，降天龍諸堡，皆禁暴掠，民悅服之。

translations.literal: He again followed Prince Yehu in pacifying the Three Han regions, reduced the Tianlong forts, and everywhere forbade looting; the people were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Prince Yehu in pacifying the Three Han regions, reduced the Tianlong forts, and everywhere forbade looting. The people were pleased and submitted.

sentences.zh: 破五里山城，請於主將，全其民，遂下甕子城、竹林寨、苦苫數島。

translations.literal: He broke Wulishan Fort, asked the commanding general to spare the people, and then took Wengzi Fort, Zhulin Stockade, and several islands of Kuchan.
translations.idiomatic: He broke Wulishan Fort, asked the commanding general to spare the people, and then took Wengzi Fort, Zhulin Stockade, and several islands of Kuchan.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其功，賜以金幣，官其子興千戶，仍賞其部曲。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his achievements, rewarded him with gold and silk, appointed his son Xing as a thousand-household commander, and also rewarded his retainers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his achievements, rewarded him with gold and silk, appointed his son Xing as a thousand-household commander, and also rewarded his retainers.

sentences.zh: 移鎮高麗平壤，帝遣使諭之曰：「彼小國負險自守，釜中之魚，非久自死，緩急可否，卿當熟思。」

translations.literal: Transferred to garrison Pyongyang in Goryeo, he received an imperial envoy who instructed him: "That small state relies on its defensible terrain and holds out on its own—it is a fish in a pot and before long will perish of itself. You must think carefully whether to press hard or hold back as circumstances allow."
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to garrison Pyongyang in Goryeo, he received an imperial envoy who told him: "That small state relies on its defensible terrain and holds out on its own—it is a fish in a pot and before long will perish of itself. You must think carefully whether to press hard or hold back as circumstances allow."

sentences.zh: 榮祖乃募民屯戍，辟地千里，盡得諸島嶼城壘，高麗遣其世子倎出降，遂以倎入朝。

translations.literal: Rongzu then recruited settlers for garrison colonies, opened up land for a thousand li, and took all the island fortresses. Goryeo sent its heir apparent Tian to surrender; Rongzu then escorted Tian to court.
translations.idiomatic: Rongzu then recruited settlers for garrison colonies, opened up land for a thousand li, and took all the island fortresses. Goryeo sent its heir apparent Tian to surrender, and Rongzu escorted Tian to court.

sentences.zh: 中統元年夏，詔榮祖詣闕，帝撫慰之曰：「卿父子勤勞於國，誠節如一。」

translations.literal: In the summer of the first year of Zhongtong, Rongzu was ordered to come to court. The emperor comforted him, saying: "Your family, father and son, have toiled for the state with unwavering loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the first year of Zhongtong (1260), Rongzu was ordered to come to court. The emperor comforted him, saying: "Your family, father and son, have toiled for the state with unwavering loyalty."

sentences.zh: 進沿邊招討使，兼北京等路征行萬戶，賜寶鞍、弓矢。

translations.literal: He was promoted to frontier pacification commissioner while retaining his post as campaign commander of the Beijing circuit and other routes, and was granted a treasured saddle, bow, and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to frontier pacification commissioner while retaining his post as campaign commander of the Beijing circuit and other routes, and was granted a treasured saddle, bow, and arrows.

sentences.zh: 還鎮，以病卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: He returned to his post, died of illness, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to his post, died of illness, aged sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 子十三人，顯者六人：通，興中府尹；

translations.literal: He had thirteen sons; six were prominent: Tong, prefect of Xingzhong;
translations.idiomatic: He had thirteen sons; six were prominent: Tong, prefect of Xingzhong;

sentences.zh: 泰，權知義、錦、川等州緫管；

translations.literal: Tai, acting overall administrator of Yizhou, Jinzhou, Chuanzhou, and other prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: Tai, acting overall administrator of Yizhou, Jinzhou, Chuanzhou, and other prefectures;

sentences.zh: 興，征東千戶；

translations.literal: Xing, thousand-household commander of the Eastern Campaign;
translations.idiomatic: Xing, thousand-household commander of the Eastern Campaign;

sentences.zh: 遇，襄陽路管軍萬戶；

translations.literal: Yu, garrison commander of the ten-thousand-household unit of Xiangyang Circuit;
translations.idiomatic: Yu, garrison commander of the ten-thousand-household unit of Xiangyang Circuit;

sentences.zh: 達，東京五處征行萬戶；

translations.literal: Da, campaign commander of the ten-thousand-household unit of the five posts of the Eastern Capital;
translations.idiomatic: Da, campaign commander of the ten-thousand-household unit of the five posts of the Eastern Capital;

sentences.zh: 廷，鎮國上將軍、中衛親軍都指揮使；

translations.literal: Ting, State-pacifying Senior General and commander of the Central Guard Imperial Army;
translations.idiomatic: Ting held the rank of State-pacifying Senior General and commanded the Central Guard Imperial Army;

sentences.zh: 璲，江西湖東道提刑按察使。

translations.literal: Sui, judicial and surveillance commissioner of the Jiangxi Huguang East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: and Sui served as judicial and surveillance commissioner of the Jiangxi Huguang East Circuit.
